<!-- emergency/index.html -->

# Emergency handbook | Universe Wallet

Suspected compromise, phishing, recovery boundaries, and transaction review - designed to work offline once saved.

# Emergency handbook

 
# Emergency handbook
 Checking whether the emergency bundle is saved for offline use…
 Save emergency guide offline Refresh cached copy Remove cached copy 
 
## How old is this guidance?
 Documentation snapshot: wallet 1.7.5.8 (source tree, unpublished). Stored release commit: cf0b6d60d00a . When offline, this page shows the date the bundle was cached at the top of every cached page. Old safety guidance must never pose as current: the banner is the difference.

## Printable checklists
 
### 1 · Suspected compromised wallet
 
- Stop signing and approving anything on the suspect device. 
- Do not send a "test transaction" from it. 
- On a clean device, create a fresh wallet and write its phrase on paper. 
- Move remaining funds and artifacts to the new wallet. 
- Remove the old wallet from the suspect device and retire the old phrase for life. 
 Full guide 

 
### 2 · Phishing and fake support
 
- Nobody legitimate ever needs your recovery words. Not support, not "validation", not upgrades. 
- Nobody legitimate needs a test signature, a screen share, or a hurry. 
- Check the origin on every approval. Look-alike domains are the con. 
- Download extensions only from the official listing. 
 Full guide 

 
### 3 · Recovery and backup boundaries
 
- Your phrase restores your keys. Anyone holding it holds your money. 
- Your password unlocks this device only. It cannot restore funds. 
- Lost password with an intact phrase: recoverable. Lost phrase with a forgotten password: not. 
 Full guide 

 
### 4 · Version identification
 
- Settings → About shows your version. 
- Store build 1.0.13 (April 2025) differs from the documented 1.7.5.8 source tree. 
- Where this site and your wallet disagree, your wallet is correct. 
 Full guide 

 
### 5 · Transaction review checklist
 
- Every output accounted for: payment + change + fee. 
- Change returns to your wallet. A stranger holding your change is theft in progress. 
- Fee far above the recommended rate: stop and reread. 
- Unreadable data signatures: treat the length warning as a stop sign. 
 Full guide · Safety Lab 

 
### 6 · Official support and reporting
 
- Documentation issues: docs-wallet issues 
- Security reports: see the repository's security policy 
- The wallet will never direct you to a support agent who asks for your phrase. 

 
 Previous Answer Center Next Payment and asset addresses

<!-- help/faq/index.html -->

# Frequently asked questions | Universe Wallet

Direct answers to the questions people actually ask, including the ones with uncomfortable answers.

- Universe Wallet 
- Help 
 
# Frequently asked questions

 
## Can Universe recover my wallet if I lose the phrase?
 Section titled “Can Universe recover my wallet if I lose the phrase?” 

 No. Not for anyone, under any circumstances. There is no account, no reset email, and no support
override. Anyone offering to do it is arranging a second theft.

 
## Can Universe reverse a transaction?
 Section titled “Can Universe reverse a transaction?” 

 No. Nobody can, including miners and the recipient. A confirmed Bitcoin transaction is final.

 
## Does Universe hold my keys?
 Section titled “Does Universe hold my keys?” 

 No. They are generated on your device, encrypted with your password, and never leave the extension.

 
## Why is my available balance lower than my total?
 Section titled “Why is my available balance lower than my total?” 

 Coins carrying assets, or coins the wallet could not check, are held back from ordinary payments. See
 Protected outputs .

 
## Why does a screen say the operation is not available?
 Section titled “Why does a screen say the operation is not available?” 

 Your build does not carry evidence for that operation. It is not an outage, a permission, or a
setting. See Why an action is unavailable .

 
## How many protocols are supported?
 Section titled “How many protocols are supported?” 

 The registry holds 42. Universe Wallet 1.7.5.8 authorizes 
0 of them. See
 What this release authorizes .

 
## Can I speed up a stuck transaction?
 Section titled “Can I speed up a stuck transaction?” 

 Not from inside Universe Wallet. There is no fee bump, no speed up, and no child-pays-for-parent. You
can mark a transaction replaceable when you create it, and the wallet does not give you a way to build
the replacement. See Read your activity .

 
## Can I sign a message of my own?
 Section titled “Can I sign a message of my own?” 

 No. Message signing appears only as an approval, in response to a request from a connected site. There
is no compose-and-sign screen.

 
## Can I connect a Ledger or Trezor?
 Section titled “Can I connect a Ledger or Trezor?” 

 No. They appear in the hardware list, disabled, marked coming soon. Keystone is the working
integration. See Hardware wallets .

 
## Which version am I running?
 Section titled “Which version am I running?” 

 Settings, then About. Read Which version you are running before you
compare it to anything on this site, because the published store build predates most of what is
documented here.

 
## Does connecting a site let it spend my coins?
 Section titled “Does connecting a site let it spend my coins?” 

 No. Connecting lets a site see one address on one network and ask you for signatures. Every signature
is approved separately. See Connection permissions .

 
## I cancelled a listing. Is it really cancelled?
 Section titled “I cancelled a listing. Is it really cancelled?” 

 Removing a listing removes it from that marketplace. It does not revoke your signature. Anyone holding
a copy can still complete it while the coin is unspent. The only certain revocation is to spend the
coin yourself. See What a signature authorizes .

 
## Is my activity private?
 Section titled “Is my activity private?” 

 No. Chain data is public by nature, and no wallet setting changes that. See
 Privacy .

 
## Can I use this on my phone?
 Section titled “Can I use this on my phone?” 

 No. Browser extensions do not run on mobile Chrome or Safari.

 
## Does it work in Firefox?
 Section titled “Does it work in Firefox?” 

 Not as a published extension. Build targets exist in the source tree; no listing exists.

 
## Why are there no screenshots on this site?
 Section titled “Why are there no screenshots on this site?” 

 Because there are no real ones to use. The product’s capture harness currently runs the wallet
offline, so every screen it captures settles into an empty or error state. Presenting a mock as a real
capture would be a false claim, so this site uses hand-authored diagrams and describes interfaces in
words instead. See Diagram conventions .

 
## Will support ever ask for my recovery phrase?
 Section titled “Will support ever ask for my recovery phrase?” 

 No. Nobody legitimate ever will, in any wallet, for any reason. See
 Phishing and impostors .

 Edit page Last updated: Nov 11, 2026

# Support and reporting | Universe Wallet

Where to ask a question, where to report a security issue, what to include, and the one thing nobody will ever ask you for.

- Universe Wallet 
- Help 
 
# Support and reporting

 Read this before contacting anyone
 Nobody will ever ask for your recovery phrase. Not through any channel below, not in a reply, not
in a direct message, not to verify your identity, not to fix your wallet. Anyone who asks is
committing fraud, no matter how the message is signed. See
 Phishing and impostors .
 Support never contacts you first.

 
 
## Before you ask
 Section titled “Before you ask” 

 Most questions have an answer already:

 

- Troubleshooting covers the common failures. 

- Frequently asked questions covers the common questions. 

- Known limitations covers the things that are missing on
purpose. 

- Why an action is unavailable covers “the screen says it is
not available”. 

 
## Documentation problems
 Section titled “Documentation problems” 

 If a page here is wrong, unclear, or missing something, that is a defect worth reporting.

 

- Open an issue on docs-wallet 

- Or use the edit link at the bottom of any page to propose the fix directly. 

 An undocumented limitation is treated as a bug in the documentation, not as an acceptable gap.

 
## Product problems
 Section titled “Product problems” 

 For behaviour that does not match this documentation, or a screen that is broken:

 

- Open an issue on the wallet repository 

 Include:

 

- your wallet version, from Settings , then About ; 

- your browser and its version; 

- the chain and network you were on; 

- what you expected and what happened; 

- a transaction id, if there is one. Transaction ids are public and safe to share. 

 Never include your recovery phrase, a private key, a screenshot showing either, or a screenshot of a
balance you would rather not publish.

 
## Security vulnerabilities
 Section titled “Security vulnerabilities” 

 Report privately, not in a public issue: legal@bitcoinuniverse.io 

 Include enough detail to reproduce, the versions affected, and what an attacker could achieve. Please
allow time for a fix before publishing.

 
## Lost funds
 Section titled “Lost funds” 

 There is no channel that can recover them. This is not a policy that can be appealed; it is a
consequence of self-custody. See
 If your wallet is compromised for what can still be done,
and act quickly if your phrase may have been exposed.

 Be aware that people who report losses publicly are contacted immediately by recovery scams. Every one
of them is fraudulent.

 
## Where the source lives
 Section titled “Where the source lives” 

 

- Product: bitcoinuniverseio/wallet 

- This documentation: bitcoinuniverseio/docs-wallet 

- Every Bitcoin Universe component: docs.bitcoinuniverse.io

<!-- help/troubleshooting/index.html -->

# Troubleshooting | Universe Wallet

The failures people actually hit, what each one means about your funds, and what to do about it.

- Universe Wallet 
- Help 
 
# Troubleshooting

 The reassuring part first
 Almost nothing in this list means your funds are at risk. Your coins are on the chain, not in the
extension, and your keys come back from your recovery phrase. The exceptions are called out
explicitly.

 
 
## The wallet will not open, or the popup is blank
 Section titled “The wallet will not open, or the popup is blank” 

 Usually a stalled extension service worker.

 

- Close the popup and reopen it from your pinned toolbar icon. 

- Open the wallet in a full tab or the side panel instead. 

- Reload the extension from the browser’s extension page. 

- Restart the browser. 

 Your funds are fine. This is a browser process problem, not a wallet problem.

 
## Balance shows zero after a restore
 Section titled “Balance shows zero after a restore” 

 Almost always the address type or derivation path, not the phrase.

 

- Try each address type: Native SegWit, Taproot, Nested SegWit, Legacy. See
 Address types . 

- If you imported from another wallet, use its preset. See
 Import an existing wallet . 

- If you used a BIP-39 passphrase, enter it. Without it you have a different wallet entirely. 

- Check an address you know is yours appears somewhere in the restored wallet. 

 
## Available balance is lower than the total
 Section titled “Available balance is lower than the total” 

 Working as intended. Some coins are protected and cannot fund a plain payment. Open the locked coins
screen to see which, and why. See Protected outputs .

 If more is protected than usual, an indexer may be lagging or unreachable, and coins that are normally
clear are being held back because unknown is treated as unsafe.

 
## A screen says the operation is not available in this build
 Section titled “A screen says the operation is not available in this build” 

 Not an outage and not a setting. Your build does not carry evidence for that operation. Nothing local
changes it. See Why an action is unavailable .

 
## A transaction has been pending for hours
 Section titled “A transaction has been pending for hours” 

 The fee rate was below what blocks are currently clearing.

 There is no fee bump in this wallet
 Universe Wallet 1.7.5.8 has no fee bump, no speed up, and no child-pays-for-parent. Your options are
to wait, or, if you marked the transaction replaceable when you created it, to build a replacement
using separate software. A transaction that is never mined is eventually dropped by nodes and the
coins become spendable again, with no fixed timetable.

 
 
## Assets do not appear, but the balance does
 Section titled “Assets do not appear, but the balance does” 

 Asset data comes from indexers, which read the chain and decide what a transaction meant. They can lag
behind confirmations.

 

- Pull down on the home screen to force a refresh. 

- Check whether the protocol is one your build can read at all. See
 What this release authorizes . 

- Look for a wallet API unreachable notice, which appears only after a health check failed and
retries every minute. 

 
## An image will not load
 Section titled “An image will not load” 

 A tile reading media unavailable means every source for that item failed. Other tiles keep loading.
Originals stay exact on chain. See Media and large portfolios .

 
## A connected site does not work
 Section titled “A connected site does not work” 

 

- Check it appears under Connected sites . If the site claims
you are connected and the wallet does not list it, the page is faking that state. Leave. 

- Check you are on the network the connection was granted for. A connection covers one address on one
network. 

- Disconnect and reconnect. 

- Reload the page. 

 
## The approval window did not appear
 Section titled “The approval window did not appear” 

 The extension service worker may be asleep, or the window opened behind your browser.

 

- Check for another browser window. 

- Open the extension from your toolbar, then retry the action on the site. 

 
## An approval says Request replaced
 Section titled “An approval says Request replaced” 

 The request changed after you looked at it, so the wallet refused rather than signing. This is the
protection working. Do not retry blindly: refresh the site’s state first, then start the action
again, and read the new request carefully.

 
## You forgot your password
 Section titled “You forgot your password” 

 Not recoverable, and not fatal. Reinstall the extension and restore from your recovery phrase. See
 Backup and recovery .

 
## Coins moved and you did not authorize it
 Section titled “Coins moved and you did not authorize it” 

 Stop reading this page. Go to
 If your wallet is compromised . Speed matters more than
diagnosis.

 
## Still stuck
 Section titled “Still stuck” 

 Support and reporting . Nobody there will ever ask for your recovery
phrase.

# Universe Wallet documentation | Universe Wallet

How to hold, receive, send, and protect Bitcoin digital artifacts in Universe Wallet, the self-custody browser wallet for Bitcoin, Dogecoin, Zcash, and Fractal Bitcoin.

# A wallet you can read before you sign it
 Universe Wallet is a self-custody browser extension for Bitcoin, Dogecoin, Zcash, and Fractal
Bitcoin. It keeps coins that carry digital artifacts out of ordinary payments, and it puts a
plain-language account of what you are about to authorize in front of every signature.

 Start here Detect my wallet version Guided journeys 
 Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished bitcoin dogecoin zcash 0 of 42 protocols authorize operations in the documented source tree. Every write action fails closed. 

 
 Enlarge 
 Home with a populated portfolio - Home answered from the synthetic portfolio fixture: real balance anatomy, ownership line, and protected-output summary with real numbers. (dark theme, 400px, wallet 1.7.5.8) 
 Home with a populated portfolio - wallet 1.7.5.8 Close 
 

 
## Read this before you trust anything else on this site
 The build published on the Chrome Web Store is 1.0.13, from 15 April 2025 . This
documentation is written against the 1.7.5.8 source tree, which has not
been submitted or published. If you installed from the store, you are running the older build,
and screens described here may not exist in it.

 In 1.7.5.8 as committed, 0 of 42 protocols 
authorize any operation. Nothing on this site should be read as a promise that a protocol action
will work in your build. The screen in your own wallet is the answer.

 The full version and release position ·
 Release notes 

 My wallet may be compromised Read the emergency steps now. No download, no sign-in, works offline once saved. 
 
## What do you need to do?
 
- Install the wallet From the real listing, verified 
- Receive Your address, safely shared 
- Send or check sending Including when a build cannot send 
- Review before you sign Read approvals like contracts 
- Protected outputs Why part of the balance holds back 
- Connect an application What a connection grants 
- Developer integration Simulated provider, generated contract 
- Emergency help Works offline once saved 

 
## Who are you?
 
- New user Installing and first steps 
- Wallet user Everyday tasks and safety 
- Developer Integrate with the provider 
- Emergency Something may be wrong

 Step-by-step walkthroughs with checkpoints, recovery paths, and progress that stays in this
browser.

## What this documentation is for
 Section titled “What this documentation is for” 

 You are holding your own keys. That means no company can move your money, and equally that no company
can give it back. Every page here is written so that believing it cannot cost you anything: where a
capability could not be verified in the wallet’s source, this site says it is not available rather
than describing how it might work.

 
- 
### Install and set up
 Which browsers work, where the real extension lives, and how to create or import a wallet without losing it a week later.
 
- 
### What a signature authorizes
 The single most valuable page here. Four kinds of approval, and the exact boundary of each one.
 
- 
### Protected outputs
 Why some of your balance will not spend, and why that is the feature rather than the fault.
 
- 
### Review before you sign
 How to read the approval screen top to bottom, and which line to check when you are in a hurry.
 
- 
### Backup and recovery
 Which loss your recovery phrase covers, which it does not, and the one situation with no way back.
 
- 
### If something is wrong
 What to do first when you think your phrase was seen, a signature went wrong, or coins moved without you.
 

 
## Where things live
 Section titled “Where things live”

 What is present, what is behind a release gate, and what does not exist at all.
 
- 
### Screen Atlas
 Every verified screenshot of the wallet, filterable and deep-linkable, with its release and provenance.

 The real wallet interface on fixture data: no keys, no network, nothing that can sign.
 
- 
### Transaction Safety Lab
 Study real approval scenarios - fees, change, protected outputs - without signing anything.
 
- 
### Protocol registry
 All 42 protocols, their chains, their intended operations, and their authorization state.
 
- 
### Known limitations
 Every limit we can state plainly, including the ones that are inconvenient to admit.
 
- 
### Provider API
 For application developers integrating a connect and sign flow with the extension.

 The failures people actually hit, and what each one means about your funds.

### Support and security reporting
 Where to ask, where to report a vulnerability, and what nobody will ever ask you for.

# Respond to a suspected compromised wallet | Universe Wallet

You contained the incident and moved remaining funds to fresh keys in the right order.

# Respond to a suspected compromised wallet

 ← All journeys 

# Respond to a suspected compromised wallet
 About 30 minutes Irreversible if wrong Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: You contained the incident and moved remaining funds to fresh keys in the right order.
 Completion looks like: Any remaining funds live under a new phrase that no suspect device or person has seen.
 If something goes wrong: Speed matters more than neatness. You can clean up after the money is safe.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Stop using the suspect wallet
 You are trying to Prevent further exposure. You should see Nothing new is signed or approved. You do Stop. Do not sign anything more, do not 'test' the wallet with small sends to check it. Before you continue, check You accept that anything the suspect device can see may already be known. What can go wrong The 'send a small test amount' reflex from compromised devices funds the attacker. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Prepare fresh keys on a clean device
 You are trying to Create a new wallet where the compromise cannot see it. You should see A new phrase exists on paper, created on a device you trust. You do Install the wallet on a clean device or profile and create a new wallet. Before you continue, check The new phrase never touches the suspect device in any form: no photo, no note, no cloud. What can go wrong Moving funds to keys the suspect device generated (or its clipboard saw) is not an escape. Reversible? No. Read twice. 
- 
### Move funds to the new wallet
 You are trying to Transfer remaining value to fresh keys. You should see Sends complete from the old wallet to the new address. You do Send everything worth keeping. Artifacts too: a moved inscription leaves the compromised keys. Before you continue, check Balance shows zero (or the amount you chose to abandon) on the old wallet. What can go wrong Leaving 'just the cheap artifacts' leaves a trail and a hook for follow-up scams. Reversible? No. Read twice. Not available here: If your build authorizes no sending, sweeping from it is impossible by design: use another wallet you control that holds the same keys, or accept the exposure and treat all funds as at risk.
 
- 
### Retire the old phrase
 You are trying to Make sure the old keys are never funded again. You should see The old phrase is out of circulation. You do Remove the wallet from the suspect device. Mark the paper phrase as burned. Before you continue, check No service, subscription, or payment card still points at the old address. What can go wrong Reusing a leaked phrase 'one more time' is how round-two losses happen. Reversible? Yes. 

 Something wrong on this page? Open a prefilled issue in the documentation repository. What travels: the page path, the release this site describes, and your own words. Nothing about your wallet, transactions, or this browser is included or stored by this site.
 Page not helpful Stale screenshot Version mismatch Unsafe or unclear wording Broken journey

# Connect to a site and review requested access | Universe Wallet

You can connect a site deliberately and read what the connection actually grants.

# Connect to a site and review requested access

 ← All journeys 

# Connect to a site and review requested access
 About 8 minutes Check before you act Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: You can connect a site deliberately and read what the connection actually grants.
 Before you start: A site you have decided to trust
 Completion looks like: The site shows as connected in the wallet, and you can name what it may and may not do.
 If something goes wrong: Disconnecting ends access instantly. Connections grant identity visibility, never spending on their own.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Start the connection from the site
 You are trying to Trigger the wallet's connection approval. You should see The wallet opens an approval naming the site's origin. You do Click the site's Connect button. Before you continue, check Read the origin in the approval. example-site.test-style names or look-alike domains mean close it. What can go wrong Connecting on a phishing page exposes your account identity to attackers, who then tailor the scam. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Read the request
 You are trying to Know what access is asked. You should see The approval states the account access requested. You do Approve or reject. Before you continue, check A connection shows your account to the site. It does not authorize spending; signatures are separate approvals. What can go wrong Approving unknown origins trains you to click through approvals, which is the habit scams harvest. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Know the unverified-origin gate
 You are trying to Recognize the state the wallet shows when it cannot verify a site. You should see A full gate: 'Unable to verify this site', with no approve control. You do Nothing to click. Close it. Before you continue, check The gate appears when the wallet's site check cannot complete. It fails closed on purpose. What can go wrong No third party can legitimately 'unlock' this gate. Instructions claiming to are the scam. Reversible? Yes. 

 Something wrong on this page? Open a prefilled issue in the documentation repository. What travels: the page path, the release this site describes, and your own words. Nothing about your wallet, transactions, or this browser is included or stored by this site.

# Create a wallet and secure its recovery material | Universe Wallet

A new wallet exists, its recovery phrase is backed up offline, and the backup status says so.

# Create a wallet and secure its recovery material

 ← All journeys 

# Create a wallet and secure its recovery material
 About 15 minutes Irreversible if wrong Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: A new wallet exists, its recovery phrase is backed up offline, and the backup status says so.
 Before you start: A private space where no camera can see your screen
 Completion looks like: Settings shows the wallet backed up, and the phrase exists only offline in your keeping.
 If something goes wrong: Until you send funds in, everything here is re-doable. Lose the phrase after funding and the money is gone; there is no reset.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Create the device password
 You are trying to Set the password that unlocks this wallet on this device. You should see Two password fields and a Continue control. You do Enter a strong password twice and continue. Before you continue, check You understand this password unlocks this device only. It is not the recovery phrase and cannot restore funds. What can go wrong A forgotten password with no phrase means reinstalling from scratch. The phrase is the real key. Reversible? No. Read twice. 
- 
### Choose the address type
 You are trying to Pick the address model for the wallet. You should see A list of address type cards; Continue stays disabled until a scan finishes. You do Keep the default unless you have a specific reason. Continue. Before you continue, check The default covers most users. Changing it later means recovery procedures. What can go wrong Importing into a mismatched address type makes balances appear missing. They are on the other path. Reversible? No. Read twice. 
- 
### Write the recovery phrase offline
 You are trying to Capture the 12 words where no camera or clipboard can reach them. You should see The phrase is shown once, masked by secure input. You do Write the words on paper in order. Verify by re-entering when asked. Before you continue, check Words exist on paper only. Never photographed, never typed into anything networked, never clipped. What can go wrong A phrase that touched a phone camera, cloud note, or password manager sync is a leaked key waiting to be used. Reversible? No. Read twice. 
- 
### Confirm backup status
 You are trying to The wallet records that the backup step is done. You should see Home shows the wallet; Settings shows backup status. You do Open Settings and confirm the backup entry reflects your paper copy. Before you continue, check Settings is the source of truth for backup state inside the wallet. What can go wrong Dismissing the backup reminder without writing the phrase is the most common permanent-loss story. Reversible? Yes. 

 Something wrong on this page? Open a prefilled issue in the documentation repository. What travels: the page path, the release this site describes, and your own words. Nothing about your wallet, transactions, or this browser is included or stored by this site.
 Page not helpful Stale screenshot Version mismatch Unsafe or unclear wording Broken journey

 Applicable release Universe Wallet 1.7.5.8

# Choose between creating and importing | Universe Wallet

You know which onboarding path matches your situation before any key exists.

# Choose between creating and importing

 ← All journeys 

# Choose between creating and importing
 About 4 minutes Standard care Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: You know which onboarding path matches your situation before any key exists.
 Before you start: The wallet installed
 Completion looks like: You can say which path applies to you and why.
 If something goes wrong: Choosing wrong here costs nothing; neither path creates anything until you complete it.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Meet the welcome screen
 You are trying to See the two paths. You should see The welcome screen offers creating a new wallet or importing one. You do Read both options. Do not decide from habit. Before you continue, check You know whether you have ever held recovery material for a Universe-compatible wallet before. What can go wrong Importing a phrase you also use in another active wallet splits custody between devices. Plan for one home per phrase. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Decide
 You are trying to Pick the honest path. You should see Clear next screen for the chosen path. You do New keys: create. Existing keys: import. Before you continue, check Create for a fresh start; import only for phrase you already control and have secured. What can go wrong Restoring from a phrase you never wrote down yourself (for example one someone gave you) hands them your money. Reversible? Yes. 

 Something wrong on this page? Open a prefilled issue in the documentation repository. What travels: the page path, the release this site describes, and your own words. Nothing about your wallet, transactions, or this browser is included or stored by this site.

# Complete a first developer connection using the simulated provider | Universe Wallet

A working integration path: detect, connect, read capabilities, handle rejection - all against the simulated provider, with a downloadable starter.

# Complete a first developer connection using the simulated provider

 ← All journeys 

# Complete a first developer connection using the simulated provider
 About 20 minutes Standard care Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: A working integration path: detect, connect, read capabilities, handle rejection - all against the simulated provider, with a downloadable starter.
 Before you start: Basic JavaScript
 Completion looks like: Your code detects the provider, handles connection and rejection, and renders unavailable states from capabilities.
 If something goes wrong: Simulation only; no wallet is touched, nothing to recover.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Detect the provider
 You are trying to Find the wallet's injected namespace. You should see Provider aliases are known: universe, tapwallet, and variants. You do Check for window.universe in the Integration Studio doctor or your code. Before you continue, check Detection says nothing about connection. It only found a candidate provider. What can go wrong Assuming detection implies consent leads to connecting without asking. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Simulate connect and rejection
 You are trying to See both outcomes. You should see The studio's fake provider answers requestAccounts with a simulated account, or a rejection. You do Run requestAccounts in the success and rejection scenarios. Before you continue, check Rejection is a normal state your UI must render, not an exception to swallow. What can go wrong Auto-retrying connection prompts train users to approve blindly. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Read capabilities and render unavailable states
 You are trying to Gate every feature on what the wallet reports. You should see getCapabilities reports this release authorizes no protocol operations. You do Call getCapabilities in the simulation and render the unavailable branch. Before you continue, check Your UI shows the unavailable state as a first-class outcome, not a disabled button. What can go wrong Promising a send the wallet refuses is a broken product and a support fire. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Download the starter and keep the loop
 You are trying to Leave with runnable code. You should see A minimal starter reflecting the contract. You do Download it from the studio and wire it into your app. Before you continue, check The starter runs without any wallet installed. What can go wrong Testing only against a real wallet hides the refusal paths your users will meet. Reversible? Yes.

# Identify the installed wallet and the right documentation release | Universe Wallet

# Identify the installed wallet and the right documentation release

 ← All journeys 

# Identify the installed wallet and the right documentation release
 About 5 minutes Standard care Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: You know exactly which build you are running and which parts of this site describe it.
 Completion looks like: You can state your wallet version and know whether this site's pages describe it.
 If something goes wrong: Nothing in this journey changes your wallet. Closing the page at any point loses nothing.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Open the wallet and its settings
 You are trying to Reach the wallet's About or Settings area, where the version is shown. You should see The wallet opens. Settings lists backup status, security, and About entries. You do Click the wallet icon, then open Settings. Before you continue, check You can see the settings list. If the wallet asks for a password, that is the unlock screen, not settings; unlock first. What can go wrong If no wallet icon exists in the browser, the extension is not installed. That is a different journey. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Read the version number
 You are trying to Find the exact version string. You should see A version like 1.0.13 or 1.7.5.8 is displayed. You do Open About (or the version row) and note the number. Before you continue, check You wrote down the exact version, not a date or a build channel. What can go wrong Some builds show the version only in the extension's detail page (browser extensions page). Both numbers are the same. Reversible? Yes. Branch: Version 1.0.13 is the published store build from April 2025. Screens on this site may not exist in it.
 
- 
### Or use Detect my wallet
 You are trying to Let this site read the version for you without you touching settings. You should see The header control reports the detected version, or says none was found. You do Click 'Detect my wallet' in this site's header. Only the version is read. Before you continue, check The control names exactly what was detected and never asks for accounts or addresses. What can go wrong An unknown version is labeled unknown. This site never guesses the nearest release. Reversible? Yes.

# Import a wallet safely | Universe Wallet

Existing keys are restored into this wallet without the phrase touching anything networked.

# Import a wallet safely

 ← All journeys 

# Import a wallet safely
 About 10 minutes Irreversible if wrong Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: Existing keys are restored into this wallet without the phrase touching anything networked.
 Before you start: Your recovery phrase or private key, already written down
 Completion looks like: The restored wallet shows the expected account and balances (or an empty account for a fresh phrase).
 If something goes wrong: Import copies; it does not move. The original phrase keeps working and must stay protected.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Choose the import source
 You are trying to Select where the keys come from. You should see A list of sources as selectable cards. You do Pick the source matching your phrase (for example a 12-word Universe-compatible wallet). Before you continue, check The source card names the wallet family the phrase belongs to. What can go wrong Wrong source means empty balances. Nothing is lost; redo with the right source. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Enter the phrase
 You are trying to Restore keys from your offline copy. You should see A grid of twelve masked inputs. You do Type words from paper. Keep secure input on. Before you continue, check The words came from paper, not from a file, a photo, or a message someone sent you. What can go wrong A phrase someone gave you 'to import' is their lever on your money. Import only phrases you generated. Reversible? No. Read twice. 
- 
### Verify what was restored
 You are trying to Confirm the account and address type match your old wallet. You should see Home shows the restored account. You do Check the receive address against the old wallet's address where possible. Before you continue, check Address type mismatch is the usual cause of 'my funds are gone' after import. They are on another derivation path. What can go wrong If balances look missing, stop sending. Recheck the address type before anything else. Reversible? Yes.

# Inspect transaction history and confirmation state | Universe Wallet

You can read your activity list and know what 'confirmed' means before you rely on a payment.

# Inspect transaction history and confirmation state

 ← All journeys 

# Inspect transaction history and confirmation state
 About 5 minutes Standard care Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: You can read your activity list and know what 'confirmed' means before you rely on a payment.
 Completion looks like: You can find a transaction's confirmation count and state what it implies.
 If something goes wrong: Reading only.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Open activity
 You are trying to See the list. You should see Transactions with direction, amount, and state. Offline builds show an explicit load failure with retry. You do Open Activity. Before you continue, check An offline error with a retry control is the honest state; an always-empty list would be a lie. What can go wrong Loading failures resolve when connectivity returns. Retry, do not re-import. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Read confirmation state
 You are trying to Know how settled a payment is. You should see Each transaction shows its confirmations (or pending). You do Open a transaction and read its state. Before you continue, check Pending means reversible by the sender; confirmed means it is in the chain and settling. What can go wrong Shipping goods for a pending payment is trusting an unconfirmed promise. Reversible? Yes.

# Install and verify the authentic extension

 ← All journeys 

# Install and verify the authentic extension
 About 10 minutes Check before you act Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: The wallet is installed from a real source and you know how to check it.
 Before you start: A Chrome-family browser
 Completion looks like: The extension is installed from the Chrome Web Store listing and its version is known.
 If something goes wrong: An extension can be removed in the browser's extensions page at any time. Installation changes nothing on chain.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Open the official store listing
 You are trying to Install from the publisher's listing, not a copy. You should see The Chrome Web Store opens on the Universe Wallet listing. You do Use the install link from this site's install page or the official site. Check the publisher name. Before you continue, check The publisher and item identifier match the official site. Fake wallets live on near-identical URLs. What can go wrong A listing with a different publisher, or any direct ZIP from chat or search ads, is the classic phishing pattern. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Add the extension
 You are trying to Complete the browser install. You should see The browser asks to confirm adding the extension. You do Confirm. Pin the icon if you want it visible. Before you continue, check Only the permissions the browser shows should appear. Nothing here should ask for your recovery phrase. What can go wrong No real wallet ever asks for existing recovery words during install. A page that does is an impostor. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Verify what you installed
 You are trying to Know the version you actually have. You should see The wallet opens on its welcome or unlock screen. You do Open settings and read the version, or use Detect my wallet here. Before you continue, check You know the version and which parts of this site describe it. What can go wrong If the wallet fails to open, remove it and reinstall from the listing; do not hunt for the missing wallet on search engines. Reversible? Yes.

# Recognize fake support and phishing | Universe Wallet

You can name the moves impostors use and the rule that defeats all of them.

# Recognize fake support and phishing

 ← All journeys 

# Recognize fake support and phishing
 About 7 minutes Check before you act Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: You can name the moves impostors use and the rule that defeats all of them.
 Completion looks like: You can state the rule: nobody legitimate ever needs your recovery words.
 If something goes wrong: Reading only.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Learn the standard moves
 You are trying to Recognize the script. You should see This page's examples. You do Read the phishing examples: fake support, urgent upgrades, 'validation' requests, look-alike extensions. Before you continue, check All of them end the same way: they want the words, a signature, or a screen share. What can go wrong Urgency is the tell. Real infrastructure problems are announced calmly, not delivered as urgent private messages. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Hold the one rule
 You are trying to One sentence beats every script. You should see Certainty. You do Say it out loud: nobody legitimate ever needs my recovery words, my seed, my screen, or a 'test' signature. Before you continue, check You would refuse a support agent asking for any of those, regardless of urgency or authority. What can go wrong Every exception you allow becomes the scam that works on you. Reversible? Yes.

# Receive funds for the first time | Universe Wallet

You requested your first payment to an address you verified in your own wallet.

# Receive funds for the first time

 ← All journeys 

# Receive funds for the first time
 About 8 minutes Check before you act Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: You requested your first payment to an address you verified in your own wallet.
 Before you start: A wallet created or imported
 Completion looks like: The payment appears in activity with its confirmation state.
 If something goes wrong: Receiving is reversible by simply sending onward. Nothing broadcast here spends your funds.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Open Receive
 You are trying to Get your receiving address. You should see The receive screen reports it is ready to receive. You do Open Receive from home. Before you continue, check The network shown in the header matches the network the payer expects. Testnet coins and mainnet coins are not interchangeable. What can go wrong Sending mainnet funds to a testnet address loses them. Read the network label. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Share the address
 You are trying to Give the payer your address or QR. You should see An address string and a QR code. You do Copy, or show the QR, or request via a payment name if configured. Before you continue, check Paste-back check: paste the address where you will send it to yourself and compare the first and last 6 characters. What can go wrong Clipboard malware swaps addresses. The paste-back check defeats the common ones. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Watch it arrive
 You are trying to See the payment and its confirmation state. You should see Activity lists the incoming payment; confirmations count up. You do Open Activity. Nothing else to do. Before you continue, check A payment is spendable per the wallet's confirmation policy; large payments deserve more confirmations before you ship goods. What can go wrong If nothing appears, verify the address the payer actually used. A wrong network or old address is the usual cause. Reversible? Yes.

# Review a transaction or PSBT before signing

 ← All journeys 

# Review a transaction or PSBT before signing
 About 10 minutes Irreversible if wrong Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: You can read a transaction review or PSBT screen and sign only what you verified.
 Completion looks like: You can name what a signature commits to before any approval.
 If something goes wrong: Refusing is always available and always safe. No signature, no consequence.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Know your build's signing availability
 You are trying to Know whether this release signs at all. You should see This source tree authorizes no signing operation; provider calls refuse before any approval. You do Check the capability status for your release. Before you continue, check A refusal is the gate, not an error to work around. What can go wrong Workarounds 'to unlock signing' are always scams. Reversible? Yes. Not available here: No signing operation is authorized in this source tree, so the approval-walk steps are educational until a release ships them.
 
- 
### Read the transaction anatomy
 You are trying to Inputs, outputs, fee, change: know what each means. You should see The review shows money in, money out, the fee, and change returning to you. You do Study the anatomy in the Safety Lab before you meet it live. Before you continue, check You can say which outputs are yours and which leave, for any transaction shown. What can go wrong The largest output not going to you is the classic theft shape. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Sign or decline
 You are trying to Commit only to what you read. You should see Approval signs exactly the displayed transaction. You do Approve if every line checks; decline otherwise. Before you continue, check Declining costs nothing, ever. What can go wrong Signing unreadable data (length warnings) commits you to something you never saw. Reversible? No. Read twice.

# Send funds safely | Universe Wallet

You know how a safe send flows, and whether your build can send at all.

# Send funds safely

 ← All journeys 

# Send funds safely
 About 12 minutes Irreversible if wrong Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: You know how a safe send flows, and whether your build can send at all.
 Before you start: Funds to send · A verified recipient address
 Completion looks like: Either the send completed with a transaction id, or your build showed the unavailable state because its release authorizes no sending.
 If something goes wrong: Before approval, a send is fully reversible: close the screen. After broadcast, nothing can pull a transaction back.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Check that this build can send
 You are trying to Know the send availability for your release. You should see Builds whose release authorizes no sending show a plain unavailable panel: 'This build cannot send'. You do Open the send screen and read what it actually offers. Before you continue, check An unavailable state is the wallet protecting you. It is not a bug and not a network outage. What can go wrong Nothing to fear here: an unauthorized build cannot send, cannot be talked into sending, and loses nothing. Reversible? Yes. Not available here: This source tree authorizes no sending operation. The journey stops at the unavailable state for this release; the remaining steps describe the authorized flow for when a release ships it.
 
- 
### Compose the payment
 You are trying to Address, amount, fee. You should see The send form with a fee selector. You do Paste the address, set the amount, choose a fee. Before you continue, check Paste-back the address. Compare fee rate to the wallet's recommendation. What can go wrong A fee far above recommendation is a signal to stop and reread every field. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Read the review screen like a contract
 You are trying to Approve exactly what you decided. You should see The transaction review: recipient, amount, fee, change. You do Read every output. The change output must return to your wallet. Before you continue, check Every output accounted for: payment + change + fee = total. What can go wrong Approving a screen you did not read is how every send scam works. No exception. Reversible? No. Read twice. 
- 
### Approve and track
 You are trying to Broadcast and watch for the transaction id. You should see A confirmation, then the transaction id in activity. You do Approve. Open activity to watch confirmations. Before you continue, check The txid in your activity is the receipt. Confirmations mean settlement. What can go wrong After broadcast there is no undo. A stuck transaction is bumped or dropped by its fee, not by support. Reversible? No. Read twice. 

 Something wrong on this page? Open a prefilled issue in the documentation repository. What travels: the page path, the release this site describes, and your own words. Nothing about your wallet, transactions, or this browser is included or stored by this site.
 Page not helpful Stale screenshot Version mismatch Unsafe or unclear wording Broken journey

# Switch chain or network safely

 ← All journeys 

# Switch chain or network safely
 About 6 minutes Check before you act Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: You can move the wallet between chains and test networks without losing track of where money applies.
 Completion looks like: You switched the active chain deliberately and can switch back.
 If something goes wrong: Switching back restores the previous view. No funds move when you switch.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Read the current chain
 You are trying to Know where you are before moving. You should see The header names the active chain and network. You do Check the header. Before you continue, check Mainnet is real money. Test networks are for practice. What can go wrong Doing mainnet actions on reflex after practicing on testnet is the common accident. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Approve a switch request
 You are trying to Move deliberately when a site or you requests a chain change. You should see The approval names both the current and the target chain. You do Approve only if the target chain makes sense for what you are doing. Before you continue, check After switching, every balance view is per-chain; the old chain's funds did not vanish. What can go wrong Sites requesting switches to obscure chains are setting up a look-alike-token trick. Reversible? Yes.

# Understand available, unavailable, and protected balance | Universe Wallet

You can explain why the wallet may show more wealth than spendable funds.

# Understand available, unavailable, and protected balance

 ← All journeys 

# Understand available, unavailable, and protected balance
 About 6 minutes Standard care Wallet 1.7.5.8 · unpublished 
 Outcome: You can explain why the wallet may show more wealth than spendable funds.
 Completion looks like: You can read the balance anatomy on home and protected outputs without surprise.
 If something goes wrong: Reading only; nothing to recover.
 
 
## All steps
 
- 
### Read the home balance anatomy
 You are trying to See total, available, and held-back amounts with the ownership line. You should see Home splits the balance when parts are not spendable. You do Compare total and available. The difference is explained below the numbers. Before you continue, check Unconfirmed incoming payments and protected outputs both reduce available funds. What can go wrong Treating the total as spendable leads to stuck payments, not losses. Reversible? Yes. 
- 
### Open protected outputs
 You are trying to See what the wallet holds back and why. You should see The protected outputs screen lists held outputs with reasons. You do Open it from settings or home. Before you continue, check Protected outputs carry artifacts (inscriptions, rare sats) that plain spending would destroy or move. What can go wrong Forcing a spend that consumes a protected output can send your art with your payment. Reversible? Yes. 

 Something wrong on this page? Open a prefilled issue in the documentation repository. What travels: the page path, the release this site describes, and your own words. Nothing about your wallet, transactions, or this browser is included or stored by this site.
 Page not helpful Stale screenshot Version mismatch Unsafe or unclear wording Broken journey

# Capability evidence | Universe Wallet

The rule that decides whether an operation ships, what counts as evidence, and how to check a claim yourself instead of taking anyone's word.

- Universe Wallet 
- Reference 
 
# Capability evidence

 Most wallets describe support by listing what the code can do. Universe Wallet does not, because a
list of what the code can do is a list of things that might work, presented as things that do.

 
## The rule
 Section titled “The rule” 

 Code existing is not support. A route existing is not availability. A parser existing is not wallet
support. 

 An operation is authorized only when the exact build carries current, verified evidence for the
complete path behind it.

 
 Six links, all of which must carry evidence bound to the exact source commit of the build. One
missing link means the operation is not authorized, and the screen says so.
 

 
## What is checked
 Section titled “What is checked” 

 The release matrix carries one row for every protocol, network, and operation combination, with UI,
provider, API, signer, indexer, health, evidence, and release-state classifications. In
the imported 1.7.5.8 source snapshot, 0 of
42 protocols have an authorized operation. This is a source baseline, not a
claim about a newly published extension.

 The local payment-instruction parser and receiving-request builder can complete their local work
without moving funds. Parsing an instruction or creating a payment request does not authorize a
payment feature or establish that a payer settled it. Remote product operations still require their
own available executor and release evidence.

 Authorization is produced for an immutable workflow run, not copied by hand into a document. The
generated readiness record contains the exact source commit, the workflow run id, individual gate
results, the protocol matrix checksum, and the exact extension artifact checksum. A go decision is
possible only when every gate succeeds, the artifact is checksum-bound, and every intended protocol
operation is evidence-backed. Zero functional coverage is always a no-go.

 
## What this means when you read a claim
 Section titled “What this means when you read a claim” 

 Any statement that Universe Wallet supports a protocol is checkable, and the way to check it is not to
ask the person who said it.

 

- Open the screen in your own wallet. 

- If the operation is not authorized in your build, the screen says so and names what is missing. 

- That screen is authoritative for you. This documentation is not, and neither is a store listing, a
social post, or a support reply. 

 
## Why the committed baseline is empty
 Section titled “Why the committed baseline is empty” 

 Deliberately. Authorization is attached at release time to one exact build. If the baseline carried
authorizations, a build could inherit a claim it never earned, which is precisely the failure the
system exists to prevent.

 So gated-blocked in the wallet’s own route inventory means “not authorized in the committed
baseline”, not “permanently unreachable”.

 
## The one campaign that has completed
 Section titled “The one campaign that has completed” 

 A qualification campaign scoped to Zerdinals and ZRunes completed on 30 August 2026 against one
candidate commit. Every release gate passed and an authorization covering thirteen operations across
those two protocols was produced. The matrix regenerated from it authorizes 26 of its 1,595 rows and
nothing outside that scope.

 That artifact has not been published. See
 Which version you are running .

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- What this release authorizes 

- Why an action is unavailable 

- The protocol registry

<!-- reference/diagram-conventions/index.html -->

# Diagram conventions | Universe Wallet

The rules every diagram on this site follows, so that a contributor can add one that matches and a reader knows what the drawing is claiming.

- Universe Wallet 
- Reference 
 
# Diagram conventions

 Every diagram here is hand-authored inline SVG, written the same way a paragraph is written. There is
no diagramming tool in the loop, and no generated image.

 
## Rules
 Section titled “Rules” 

 One idea per diagram. If a second idea needs saying, it gets a second diagram.

 Colour carries meaning, never decoration. The page is near-neutral. Exactly one chromatic accent
exists, and it is reserved for warnings, irreversible actions, and blocked states. If a diagram uses
it anywhere else, colour stops meaning anything and a reader stops noticing it where it matters.

 Colour is never the only signal. A held-back coin is drawn with a hatch pattern and labelled
Protected. A dangerous path is drawn in the accent and says so in words. Remove the colour and
every diagram still reads. This is WCAG 1.4.1, and it is also just better drawing.

 Theme-aware by construction. Diagrams are inline SVG using the site’s CSS custom properties, so
they follow the theme toggle exactly, including for a reader who chose light while their operating
system is dark. They are not images with a baked-in palette.

 No markers for arrowheads. A &#x3C;marker> cannot reliably inherit the referencing path’s colour
across a theme switch. Arrowheads are explicit paths with their own class.

 Accessible. Every diagram carries role="img" and aria-labelledby pointing at a &#x3C;title> and a
 &#x3C;desc> . The description says what the diagram shows, not what it looks like, so a reader who cannot
see it gets the whole point rather than a shape inventory.

 Legible on a phone. A diagram scrolls inside its own focusable frame on a narrow screen rather
than shrinking until its labels are unreadable. The frame is keyboard reachable.

 Synthetic values only. Every address, balance, transaction id, outpoint, and site name is
invented. Nothing in any diagram comes from a real wallet.

 No screenshots. This documentation contains none. The product’s own capture harness currently runs
the wallet offline, so every screen it captures settles into an empty or error state, and presenting a
mock as a real capture would be a false claim in image form. Diagrams and written descriptions are the
honest substitute. See Known limitations .

 No em dashes, no emoji. The same copy rules as the prose, enforced by
 npm run check:copy .

 
## The diagrams
 Section titled “The diagrams” 

 

 Diagram Explains Appears on Address lanes One phrase, four address types, and why there is no asset address Payment and asset addresses Protected outputs Why an asset-bearing coin never funds a plain payment Protected outputs Signature scope Four kinds of approval and the boundary of each What a signature authorizes Transaction anatomy Inputs, outputs, fee, and change, with arithmetic that adds up Inputs, outputs, fees, change Connection permissions What a site is granted, what it never is, and how access ends Connection permissions Backup and recovery Which loss the phrase covers, and the one it does not Backup and recovery Review anatomy The order the approval screen is built in Review a transaction Release evidence Why an action appears only when evidence covers the path Capability evidence 

 
## Adding one
 Section titled “Adding one” 

 Add a component under src/components/diagrams/ , use the dg- classes defined in
 src/styles/theme.css , wrap it in the Diagram component with a title and a caption, and run
 npm run check:diagrams , which fails on a diagram missing a title or a description.

<!-- reference/glossary/index.html -->

# Glossary | Universe Wallet

The words this documentation uses, defined precisely, including the ones that mean something different here than elsewhere.

- Universe Wallet 
- Reference 
 
# Glossary

 Address. A destination that can receive coins. One recovery phrase produces many. See
 Address types .

 Approval. The screen the wallet puts in front of you before it signs anything. See
 Review a transaction .

 Authorized. In this documentation, an operation the exact build you are running carries evidence
for. Not the same as implemented. See Capability evidence .

 Available balance. The part of your total balance that can fund an ordinary payment. Lower than
the total when coins are protected.

 BIP-39. The standard that turns a list of words into a wallet. The reason a phrase from one wallet
works in another.

 Change. An output that returns the remainder of a spent coin to an address you own. A real
payment to yourself, not a leftover.

 Confidence mark. EXACT, ESTIMATED, or UNKNOWN, attached to each interpreted fact on an approval.
See Confidence marks .

 Confirmation. Inclusion of your transaction in a block. Each subsequent block adds one.

 Connection. Permission for a site to see one address on one network and to ask you for
signatures. Never permission to spend. See
 Connection permissions .

 Derivation path. The recipe that turns a phrase into a specific set of keys, written like
 m/84'/0'/0'/0 . Change it and you get a different, equally valid wallet.

 Dust. An output too small to be worth spending, because spending it would cost more than it holds.

 Gate. A condition a screen sits behind. A protocol gate opens only when the release authorized
that operation. See Why an action is unavailable .

 Idle window. How long a connection survives without use. Resets on every use. 24 hours, 7 days,
30 days as the default, or until you disconnect.

 Input. A coin being spent by a transaction. Consumed whole.

 Inscription. Data written to the chain and treated as attached to one specific satoshi. Lives on
one output.

 Mempool. The waiting area for broadcast transactions that are not yet in a block.

 Output. A newly created coin. The recipient’s payment and your change are both outputs.

 Protected. A coin the wallet will not select for an ordinary payment, because it carries an
asset, a rare-satoshi candidate, a lock you set, or because the check could not complete. See
 Protected outputs .

 PSBT. Partially signed Bitcoin transaction. A draft someone else built that can collect signatures
over time. See Review a PSBT .

 RBF, replace by fee. A network convention allowing an unconfirmed transaction to be replaced by a
higher-fee version. Universe Wallet can mark a transaction as replaceable and does not provide a way
to build the replacement .

 Recovery phrase. The words that are your wallet. Not a hint, not a reset code. See
 Backup and recovery .

 Sat, satoshi. The smallest unit of bitcoin. One hundred million to a bitcoin.

 Sat per vB. The fee rate. Satoshis paid per virtual byte of transaction size.

 Sighash. The part of a signature that says how much of a transaction it commits to. The difference
between an approval that cannot change and one anyone can finish. See
 What a signature authorizes .

 Testnet, signet. Networks with worthless coins, for practice. Their addresses are not
interchangeable with mainnet.

 Total balance. Everything you hold, including protected coins.

 Transaction id, txid. The public identifier of a transaction. Safe to share, and verifiable by
anyone.

 UTXO, unspent transaction output. A coin you own that has not yet been spent. What “your balance”
is actually made of. See Inputs, outputs, fees, change .

 Virtual byte, vB. The unit transaction size is measured in for fee purposes.

 Watch-only. A wallet holding public keys only, which can see everything and sign nothing. See
 Watch-only wallets .

# Known limitations | Universe Wallet

Every limit of Universe Wallet 1.7.5.8 that could be established from source, including the ones that are inconvenient to admit.

- Universe Wallet 
- Reference 
 
# Known limitations

 An undocumented limitation is treated as a bug in the documentation. If you find one missing, report
it through support .

 
## Release position
 Section titled “Release position” 

 

- The published build is 1.0.13, from April 2025. This documentation describes the
1.7.5.8 source tree, which has not been submitted or published. See
 Which version you are running . 

- No protocol operation is authorized in the committed baseline. 
0 of 42. Authorization is attached at release
time from evidence, and the baseline carries none on purpose. 

- Ordinary Bitcoin sending is behind a release gate , exactly like a protocol operation. Whether
it works in your build was decided by that build. 

 
## Transactions
 Section titled “Transactions” 

 

- There is no fee bump, no speed up, and no child-pays-for-parent. You can mark a transaction
replaceable at creation, and the wallet gives you no way to build the replacement. A payment sent at
too low a rate can only be waited out or replaced using separate software. 

- There is no standalone coin control screen. Manual coin selection exists inside the PSBT
approval flow, where the request allows it. It is not offered on the ordinary send screen. 

- The transaction inspector does not decode PSBTs. It looks up an existing transaction by id. A
PSBT is reviewed on its approval screen. 

 
## Signing
 Section titled “Signing” 

 

- You cannot compose and sign your own message. Message signing appears only as an approval, in
response to a request from a connected site. 

- Raw data signing is off by default and requires a typed confirmation to enable, by design. 

 
## Keys and devices
 Section titled “Keys and devices” 

 

- Ledger and Trezor cannot be connected. They appear in the hardware list, disabled, marked coming
soon. Keystone is the one working integration. 

- The hardware wallet feature is marked experimental in the product. Verify addresses on the
device and start small. 

- Watch-only import is behind developer mode , and takes an extended public key by QR. There is no
flow for watching a single pasted address. 

- New wallets are 12 words. Longer phrases from other wallets import fine. 

 
## Networks and protocols
 Section titled “Networks and protocols” 

 

- Babylon and Cosmos are not selectable. The registry carries a Babylon entry and the source tree
carries Babylon screens, whose design obligation is recorded as not intended, meaning only the
unavailable state ships. 

- Firefox is not published. Build targets exist in the source tree. No listing exists. 

- Safari and mobile browsers are not supported , and cannot be, because browser extensions do not
run there. 

 
## Data and display
 Section titled “Data and display” 

 

- Asset data depends on indexers , which read the chain and decide what a transaction meant. They
can lag behind confirmations, and a protocol the wallet does not index cannot be classified or
protected. 

- Fiat display depends on a current Universe price source. When no current price is available,
amounts show without a fiat figure rather than with a stale or third-party number. 

- The language picker offers four languages , English, Chinese, Japanese, and Spanish, while seven
locale files ship inside the artifact. 

 
## Custody and settings
 Section titled “Custody and settings” 

 

- Settings do not travel with the phrase. Contacts, labels, locked coins, limits, and connected
sites are device-local. After a restore, re-create them. 

- A wallet cannot make chain data private. Addresses and transactions are public by nature. See
 Privacy . 

- Protection is a Universe Wallet behaviour, not a property of your keys. Import the same phrase
into another wallet and every coin becomes ordinary money again. 

 
## Things this documentation could not verify
 Section titled “Things this documentation could not verify” 

 Stated here rather than described elsewhere, because an unverifiable claim in a wallet manual is a
liability.

 

- No screenshots of the product exist in this documentation. The product’s own capture harness
currently runs the wallet offline, so every screen it captures settles into an empty or error state.
Rather than present a mock as a real capture, this site uses hand-authored diagrams and describes
interfaces in words. 

- The behaviour of the published 1.0.13 build could not be verified. Its source is not the tree
this documentation was written against. Where this site and your wallet disagree, your wallet is
correct. 

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Supported features 

- Troubleshooting

# Release notes | Universe Wallet

What changed between the wallet builds this documentation can verify, and what has and has not reached users.

- Universe Wallet 
- Reference 
 
# Release notes

 Only one build has ever reached users
 The Chrome Web Store item has served 1.0.13 since 15 April 2025. Every version below exists as a
candidate in the source tree and in the release list, and none of them has been published. See
 Which version you are running .

 
 
## What is published
 Section titled “What is published” 

 Version Date Where 1.0.13 15 April 2025 Chrome Web Store item fjalkkkbjffhgdoheannkodafhemfdba 

 This documentation was not written against 1.0.13 and cannot describe it accurately. Its source is not
the tree used here.

 
## What exists as candidates
 Section titled “What exists as candidates” 

 Version State 1.7.5.8 Current source tree. 0 of 42 protocols authorized in the committed baseline. Not submitted. 1.7.5.6 Production readiness record exists, bound to one commit and one workflow run. 1.7.5.5, 1.7.5.4 Production release records and protocol matrices exist for both. 

 Candidate builds are published as pre-releases on the
 wallet releases page , named by their exact
commit. A pre-release is a candidate that has been built, not a build that has been authorized.

 
## The one qualification that completed
 Section titled “The one qualification that completed” 

 On 30 August 2026, a campaign scoped to Zerdinals and ZRunes completed against a single candidate
commit. Every release gate passed, and an authorization covering thirteen operations across those two
protocols was produced. The regenerated matrix authorizes 26 of its 1,595 rows and nothing outside
that scope.

 Submission remains blocked because the Chrome Web Store publishing credential is not available to the
repository.

 
## What changed in 1.7.5.8 that is visible to a user
 Section titled “What changed in that is visible to a user” 

 Verifiable from the source tree and its own records:

 

- Risk rows in the approval popover now open with a chip reading Warning or Critical . Before
1.7.5.8 the severity was carried only by colour, which failed the rule that colour
must never be the only signal. 

- The route inventory records 113 routes across 47 areas, with 15 approval variants, laying out at
popup, side panel, and tab widths. 

 
## How to read a release claim
 Section titled “How to read a release claim” 

 A version number tells you which code was built. It does not tell you which operations that build
authorizes. Those are separate facts, and the second one is the one that affects you. See
 Capability evidence .

# Supported features | Universe Wallet

What is present with no gate, what is present behind a release gate, and what does not exist at all in Universe Wallet 1.7.5.8.

- Universe Wallet 
- Reference 
 
# Supported features

 Three columns matter here, and mixing them up is how documentation misleads people.

 

- Present means the screen exists with no protocol gate. It is in every build. 

- Gated means the screen exists behind a protocol gate. Whether it works depends on what your
build authorized. In the 1.7.5.8 baseline, nothing is authorized. 

- Not available means it is not in this build at all. Not hidden, not disabled: absent. 

 
## Platform
 Section titled “Platform” 

 Item State Browser Chrome 88 or later, Manifest V3. Other Chromium browsers run the same package. Firefox Not available. Build targets exist; no listing is published. Safari and mobile Not available. Views Popup, side panel, and full-tab. All 112 routes lay out at all three widths. Languages in the picker English, Chinese, Japanese, Spanish. Seven locale files ship in the artifact. 

 
## Keys and accounts
 Section titled “Keys and accounts” 

 Capability State Create wallet Present. 12-word BIP-39 phrase with a confirmation check. Import phrase Present. Presets for Unisat, Sparrow, Xverse, Ordinals Wallet, and others. Optional BIP-39 passphrase and custom derivation path. Import private key Present. WIF and hex. Address types Present. Native SegWit, Nested SegWit, Taproot, Legacy, plus two BIP-44 compatibility variants. Multiple wallets and accounts Present, with renaming. Keystone hardware Present. Air-gapped QR and USB. Marked experimental in the product. Ledger, Trezor Not available. Listed, disabled, shown as coming soon. Watch-only, cold wallet Present, behind developer mode. Extended public key by QR. No paste-an-address flow. 

 
## Transactions
 Section titled “Transactions” 

 Capability State Send Gated on bitcoin/send and bitcoin/broadcast . Batch send Gated on bitcoin/send . Consolidation Gated on bitcoin/send . Fee control Present. Live presets and a custom sat/vB rate. Mark transaction replaceable Present. Off by default, stated on the review screen. Fee bump, speed up, RBF replacement, CPFP Not available. No flow exists to replace or accelerate a broadcast transaction. Manual coin selection Present inside the PSBT approval flow. No standalone coin control screen. Locked coins list Present, no gate. Coin health Present, no gate. Asset protection Present. Asset-bearing outputs never fund plain sends. Payment requests Present. Amount and note in the QR and a copyable link. Transaction review Present. Impact summary with EXACT, ESTIMATED, and UNKNOWN marks, inputs, outputs, fee, and raw transaction. Transaction inspector Present. Looks up an existing transaction by id. It does not decode a PSBT. Spending limits and whitelist Present, off by default. 

 The two rows worth re-reading
 There is no fee bump and no child-pays-for-parent anywhere in this build. And ordinary sending
is behind a release gate , like every protocol operation. Neither of these is what people assume.

 
 
## Connected applications
 Section titled “Connected applications” 

 Capability State Connection scope Present. One selected account per site, per network. Per-request approval Present. Every signature is approved separately. Expiry Present. Idle windows of 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days as default, or until disconnected. Connection audit and revoke Present. Local risk scoring, one-step revoke. Message signing, site initiated Present, as an approval. Text with scam-language scanning. Message signing, user initiated Not available. No screen for composing your own message. Raw data signing Present, off by default, typed confirmation to enable. PSBT signing Present, as an approval. Single and multiple. Chain and network switch requests Present, as approvals. Phishing filtering Present. Local blocking rules shipped in the extension. 

 
## Protocols
 Section titled “Protocols” 

 42 protocols across Bitcoin, Dogecoin, Zcash, Fractal, and a Cosmos entry. This
release authorizes 0 of them. That is the size of the registry, not a
list of what your build can do. See The protocol registry and
 What this release authorizes .

 Babylon and Cosmos are not selectable in the network picker and their routes carry a design
obligation of not intended. Treat them as unavailable.

 
## Security
 Section titled “Security” 

 Capability State Auto-lock Present. 30 seconds to 4 hours, default 30 minutes. Immediate lock Present. Password change Present. Security dashboard Present, no gate. Recovery tracking, login history, session log, phishing URL checker. Request integrity Present. A request that changed after you saw it is blocked as Request replaced.
