<!-- safety/compromised-wallet/index.html -->

# If your wallet is compromised | Universe Wallet

What to do first, in order, when you think your phrase was seen, a signature went wrong, or coins moved without you.

- Universe Wallet 
- Safety 
 
# If your wallet is compromised

 This page is written to be read quickly, by someone who is not calm. Start at the situation that
matches yours.

 Before anything else
 Do not enter your recovery phrase into any site, tool, or person offering to help. Every recovery
service is a second theft. There is no legitimate one, anywhere, for any wallet.

 
 
## Your recovery phrase may have been seen
 Section titled “Your recovery phrase may have been seen” 

 This is the most serious case, because access cannot be taken back.

 A phrase cannot be made secret again. Changing your password does nothing. Locking the wallet does
nothing. Uninstalling does nothing. The only fix is to move everything to keys that person has never
seen.

 

- Create a brand new wallet, from a new phrase. On a device you believe is clean. Write the new
phrase down on paper. 

- Move your plain currency first. It is the easiest to sweep and the most likely to be taken. 

- Move your assets next , using the flow built for each asset type. If those flows are not
available in your build, you cannot move assets from inside this wallet, and you should still move
the currency. See Why an action is unavailable . 

- Do not send anything back to the old wallet , ever, including change from an unrelated
transaction. 

- Assume anything left behind will be taken. Prioritise by value, not by convenience. 

 If your holdings are large and the exposure is recent, moving currency in a single high-fee
transaction is usually worth it. An attacker who is watching will race you.

 
## You approved something and now regret it
 Section titled “You approved something and now regret it” 

 

- Open Connected sites and disconnect the site. This
stops further requests. It does not undo what you already signed. 

- Check Activity for what actually happened. 

- Work out what the signature was. A payment is done. A message signature moved nothing. A
partial signature may still be outstanding and completable by someone else. See
 What a signature authorizes . 

- If a partial signature is outstanding , the only certain revocation is to spend the committed
coin yourself, into a transaction you control, so the offer can no longer be completed. 

 
## Coins moved without you
 Section titled “Coins moved without you” 

 

- Check whether it was really unauthorized. A change output returning to your own address looks
like an outgoing transaction to a stranger. Check whether the destination is one of yours. 

- If it genuinely was not you, your keys are compromised. Follow the phrase-exposed procedure
above immediately. Do not investigate first. 

- Record the transaction ids before you do anything else. They are the only evidence, and they
are public. 

 
## You installed something that was not the real wallet
 Section titled “You installed something that was not the real wallet” 

 

- Remove it. 

- If you entered your phrase into it, treat the phrase as fully exposed and follow the first
procedure above. 

- If you never entered a phrase into it, no key material was ever there and you are fine. 

 
## What nobody can do for you
 Section titled “What nobody can do for you” 

 

- Reverse a confirmed transaction. 

- Freeze funds at another address. 

- Recover a lost phrase. 

- Identify who took the coins in a way that gets them back. 

 The second wave
 People who lose funds publicly are targeted immediately by recovery scams. If you post about a loss,
expect messages from accounts impersonating support, offering blockchain forensics, or claiming to
know a validator who can reverse it. All of them are the same scam. Post the transaction id if you
want, and never post an address you still use, and never speak to anyone who contacts you first.

 
 
## Afterwards
 Section titled “Afterwards” 

 

- Review Security model and decide what you would do
differently. 

- Consider hardware signing for long-term holdings. 

- Keep experimenting money in a separate wallet from savings. 

 
## Reporting
 Section titled “Reporting” 

 If you believe the loss came from a flaw in the product rather than from an exposed phrase, report it
to legal@bitcoinuniverse.io . See Support and reporting .

<!-- safety/phishing/index.html -->

# Phishing and impostors | Universe Wallet

The small number of attacks that account for almost all losses, the one rule that defeats most of them, and what the wallet does and does not filter.

- Universe Wallet 
- Safety 
 
# Phishing and impostors

 
## The one rule
 Section titled “The one rule” 

 Nobody legitimate ever needs your recovery phrase. 

 Not support. Not a verification step. Not a wallet upgrade. Not an airdrop claim. Not a migration
tool. Not a security check. Not the person helping you recover funds. There is no exception, in any
wallet, ever.

 If you follow only this rule, you avoid most of the ways people lose everything.

 
## The attacks that actually work
 Section titled “The attacks that actually work” 

 
### The counterfeit extension
 Section titled “The counterfeit extension” 

 A store listing that copies the name, icon, and description. It asks you to import your phrase and
takes everything the moment you do.

 Defence: install only from the store listing with item id
 fjalkkkbjffhgdoheannkodafhemfdba . Names can be copied. Ids cannot. See
 Install .

 
### Support that contacts you first
 Section titled “Support that contacts you first” 

 Someone appears in a reply, a direct message, or a chat channel, offering to help with a problem you
mentioned. They are friendly, they are competent, and eventually they need your phrase or a “sync
code”.

 Defence: real support never contacts you first and never needs your phrase. Go to
 Support yourself.

 
### The look-alike site
 Section titled “The look-alike site” 

 A site one character away from the real one, or a sponsored search result above it. Everything works
until the signature request, which does something other than what the page says.

 Defence: bookmark the sites you use and reach them from your bookmarks. Read the origin line the
wallet shows, which comes from the browser and cannot be faked by the page.

 
### The unreadable signature
 Section titled “The unreadable signature” 

 A request that is raw data rather than readable text, or a transaction whose effect you cannot
explain. Sometimes framed as “just verifying your wallet”.

 Defence: if you cannot say in one sentence what the request does, reject it. See
 What a signature authorizes .

 
### The address swap
 Section titled “The address swap” 

 Malware that replaces an address in your clipboard between copying and pasting. The ends often look
plausible.

 Defence: compare the first four and last four characters after pasting, every time.

 
### The urgent deadline
 Section titled “The urgent deadline” 

 A mint closing, a claim expiring, a compromise you must fix in the next ten minutes. Urgency exists to
stop you reading.

 Defence: treat urgency itself as the warning. Nothing legitimate is destroyed by taking five
minutes to check.

 
## What the wallet does
 Section titled “What the wallet does” 

 

- Blocks known phishing domains through rules that ship inside the extension, applied locally rather
than by sending your browsing anywhere. 

- Screens signature request text for scam-language patterns and warns you. 

- Shows the origin the browser reports, not a name the page chose. 

- Provides a phishing URL checker in the security dashboard. 

 
## What the wallet cannot do
 Section titled “What the wallet cannot do” 

 

- Recognise a site that is new, or convincing, or targeted at you specifically. 

- Tell whether the deal you are signing is a good one. 

- Stop you approving something after it warned you. 

 Filtering catches the known. Your reading catches the rest.

 
## If you already did
 Section titled “If you already did” 

 Go to If your wallet is compromised . Speed matters more than
diagnosis.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Security model 

- Manage connections

<!-- safety/privacy/index.html -->

# Privacy | Universe Wallet

What leaves your device by design, what never does, what a connected site can learn, and the limit no wallet can pass.

- Universe Wallet 
- Safety 
 
# Privacy

 
## Never leaves your device
 Section titled “Never leaves your device” 

 

- Your recovery phrase and private keys. Generated locally, stored encrypted with your password. No
Universe system ever receives them. 

- Your password. 

- Device-local settings: contacts, address labels, locked coins, spending limits, and connected-site
records. 

 
## Leaves your device, by design
 Section titled “Leaves your device, by design” 

 

- Your addresses , to Universe-operated APIs and indexers, because balance, asset, and activity
data is answered per address. This is how every light wallet works. Universe answers these reads
from its own infrastructure rather than from third-party data providers. 

- Signed transactions you broadcast , to the network, where they are public permanently. 

- Requests for media and prices , to Universe-operated services. 

 
## The limit no wallet can pass
 Section titled “The limit no wallet can pass” 

 Bitcoin, Dogecoin, and transparent Zcash are public ledgers. Anyone who learns one of your addresses
can see everything that address has ever done, and can often infer which other addresses belong to
you from how coins were spent together.

 A wallet cannot make chain activity private
 No setting in Universe Wallet changes this, and any wallet that claims otherwise is describing
something the chain does not do. The mitigations below reduce linkage. They do not create privacy.

 
 
## Practical mitigations
 Section titled “Practical mitigations” 

 

- Use a fresh receiving address per payment. Reuse links every payment to one identity. 

- Keep addresses off social media. One public post ties an address to a person permanently. 

- Separate wallets by purpose. Long-term holdings in one, experimenting in another. Coins spent
together are assumed to share an owner. 

- Be careful with consolidation. Combining many coins in one transaction tells observers they all
belonged to you. Sometimes that is fine. Decide deliberately. 

- Fiat display. Price requests are made to Universe-operated services. When no current price is
available, amounts are shown without a fiat figure rather than with a stale or third-party number. 

 
## What a connected site can learn
 Section titled “What a connected site can learn” 

 A connected site sees the one address you shared with it, and what you sign for it. Nothing else. It
cannot see your other accounts, your other networks, or your balances at addresses you did not share.

 An unconnected site cannot read anything from the wallet at all.

 Phishing filtering runs locally, through blocking rules that ship inside the extension, rather than by
sending your browsing to a service.

 
## The authoritative statement
 Section titled “The authoritative statement” 

 The privacy policy is the complete, current statement of data
handling, and it applies where this summary and the policy differ.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Connection permissions 

- Security model

<!-- safety/security-model/index.html -->

# Security model | Universe Wallet

Where your keys live, what protects them, what Universe can and cannot do, and which decisions stay yours no matter what the product does.

- Universe Wallet 
- Safety 
 
# Security model

 
## Where your keys live
 Section titled “Where your keys live” 

 Your recovery phrase and private keys are generated inside the extension, encrypted with your
password, and stored only on your device. They are never sent to Universe or to anyone else. Signing
happens inside the extension, or on your hardware device for hardware accounts.

 
## What Universe can do
 Section titled “What Universe can do” 

 

- Serve chain data, asset indexes, and media from Universe-operated infrastructure. 

- Block known phishing sites before they load, and screen signature requests for scam language. 

- Ship releases in which each protocol action is enabled only with current, verified, end-to-end
evidence. 

 
## What Universe cannot do
 Section titled “What Universe cannot do” 

 

- Move, freeze, or recover your funds. 

- Reverse a confirmed transaction. Nobody can. 

- Restore a lost recovery phrase. There is no account, no reset email, and no support override. 

 Anyone claiming to be Universe support and asking for your phrase is committing fraud
 There is no scenario, no upgrade, no verification, and no recovery procedure that requires your
recovery phrase to be given to anyone. See Phishing and impostors .

 
 
## The defences in the product
 Section titled “The defences in the product” 

 Password and auto-lock. The wallet locks itself after your chosen idle time, from 30 seconds to 4
hours. The default is 30 minutes, and the lock-time screen recommends 5 minutes. Lock Immediately sits
at the bottom of Settings.

 Approval on everything. No connected site can spend or sign without a request you read and accept.
See Connection permissions .

 Asset-aware spending. Coins carrying assets never fund ordinary payments. See
 Protected outputs .

 Request integrity. An approval is bound to the exact request that opened it. Approval authority is
computed once per request identity and re-checked synchronously at every signing entry point. A
request that changed after you saw it is blocked as Request replaced , rather than signed.

 Optional hard limits. Whitelists and spending caps, available in the security dashboard and
enforced by the send flow. Off by default.

 Raw-data signing off by default. Enabling it requires a typed confirmation. See
 Sign a message .

 Evidence-gated releases. An operation reaches you only when the exact build carries current
qualification evidence for the complete path. See
 Capability evidence .

 
## What the model does not cover
 Section titled “What the model does not cover” 

 Be clear about the boundary, because a security model that implies more than it delivers is worse than
none.

 

- A compromised computer. Malware with access to your browser profile and your keystrokes can
reach an unlocked wallet. Hardware signing raises this bar considerably. See
 Hardware wallets . 

- Your recovery phrase on paper. Nothing in software protects a piece of paper. 

- A signature you gave deliberately. The wallet can make a request readable. It cannot decide for
you whether the deal is a good one. 

- An outstanding partial signature. Once given, it can be completed by anyone holding it while the
coin is unspent. See
 What a signature authorizes . 

- Another wallet using the same phrase. Protections here are Universe Wallet behaviours, not
properties of your keys. 

 
## The decisions that stay yours
 Section titled “The decisions that stay yours” 

 The product cannot protect the phrase written on your paper, the address you paste, or the request you
approve without reading. Its job is to make each of those decisions clear at the moment you take it.
The words in the review are chosen so that you can explain what will happen before you sign.

 If you cannot explain what a request does, that is the signal to reject it.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- If your wallet is compromised 

- Privacy 

- Security dashboard

<!-- safety-lab/index.html -->

# Transaction and Approval Safety Lab | Universe Wallet

Study real transaction and approval scenarios - fees, change, protected outputs, sighash - without signing anything.

# Transaction and Approval Safety Lab

 
# Transaction and Approval Safety Lab
 Every scenario here is a fixture generated from the wallet's own approval view models over synthetic data. Nothing in this laboratory signs, broadcasts, or contacts anything: it exists so that the first time you meet an unusual approval, it is not the first time you have seen its shape.
 

## Every scenario, in plain text
 The same content without JavaScript, for screen readers, search engines, and printing.
 
### When the change does not come back to your wallet
 The wallet's summary: “This sends BTC” (review)
 
- 1 input needs your signature. 
- 2 outputs go outside this wallet; 0 return to you. 
 Inputs: yours (10000 sats);
 Outputs: leaves your wallet (8000 sats); leaves your wallet (1500 sats);
 Fee: 500 sats at 2 sat/vB. No bump capability.

#### What to check
 
- The second output goes to an address that is not yours. 
- Change must return to your wallet. A stranger holding your change can collect it. 

 
### When the wallet cannot summarize a request safely
 The wallet's summary: “Cannot summarize safely” (danger)
 
- The wallet does not have enough decoded PSBT data to make a short summary. 
 Inputs: 
 Outputs: leaves your wallet (8000 sats); change to you (1500 sats);
 Fee: 500 sats at 2 sat/vB. No bump capability.

#### What to check
 
- When decoded data is missing, the wallet refuses to summarize instead of guessing. 
- A request the wallet cannot read is a request you should not sign. 

 
### A payment with several recipients
 The wallet's summary: “This sends BTC” (review)
 
- 1 input needs your signature. 
- 3 outputs go outside this wallet; 0 return to you. 
 Inputs: yours (10000 sats);
 Outputs: leaves your wallet (4000 sats); leaves your wallet (3000 sats); change to you (2500 sats);
 Fee: 500 sats at 2 sat/vB. No bump capability.

#### What to check
 
- A transaction can pay many recipients at once; read every output. 
- Your change is an output too. Anything that is not yours is a payment. 

 
### An ordinary send
 The wallet's summary: “This sends BTC” (review)
 
- 1 input needs your signature. 
- 2 outputs go outside this wallet; 0 return to you. 
 Inputs: yours (10000 sats);
 Outputs: leaves your wallet (8000 sats); change to you (1500 sats);
 Fee: 500 sats at 2 sat/vB. No bump capability.

#### What to check
 
- One output leaves the wallet, one output returns to it as change. 
- The fee is the difference between what goes in and what comes out. 
- Signing only this input at SIGHASH_ALL commits to the whole transaction. 

 
### A rare-sat transfer keeps its protected output first
 The wallet's summary: “This moves protected Rare Sats” (review)
 
- 1 input needs your signature. 
- 1 output goes outside this wallet; 0 return to you. 
- Protected Rare Sats move together in their complete UTXO. Separate cardinal BTC pays the network fee. 
- Protected UTXO: cccccccccccc…cccccccc:2. 
- Protected Rare-Sat composition: The sat you are sending rides on the first input and must lead the outputs unchanged.. 
 Inputs: yours (10000 sats);
 Outputs: leaves your wallet (10000 sats);
 Fee: 500 sats at 2 sat/vB. No bump capability.

#### What to check
 
- Protected assets keep their position: the protected output leads. 
- If a request reorders or splits the protected output, the asset can be lost. 

 
### A PSBT that spends inputs you do not own
 The wallet's summary: “This signs a Bitcoin transaction” (ok)
 
- 1 input needs your signature. 
- 1 output goes outside this wallet; 0 return to you. 
 Inputs: not yours (5000 sats); yours (10000 sats);
 Outputs: leaves your wallet (14000 sats);
 Fee: 1000 sats at 2 sat/vB. No bump capability.

#### What to check
 
- A PSBT can bundle inputs from many owners. 
- Only inputs marked as yours are signed; everything else is someone else’s money in the same transaction. 

 
### What a looser signature commits to
 The wallet's summary: “This signs a Bitcoin transaction” (review)
 
- 1 input needs your signature. 
- 2 outputs go outside this wallet; 0 return to you. 
 Inputs: yours (10000 sats, SIGHASH_SINGLE - commits this input to one output only);
 Outputs: leaves your wallet (8000 sats); change to you (1500 sats);
 Fee: 500 sats at 2 sat/vB. No bump capability.

#### What to check
 
- SIGHASH_SINGLE commits your input to only one output, leaving other outputs free to change. 
- Marketplaces use this for listings. Read which output is yours before signing one. 

 
### An output you did not expect
 The wallet's summary: “This sends BTC” (review)
 
- 1 input needs your signature. 
- 2 outputs go outside this wallet; 0 return to you. 
 Inputs: yours (10000 sats);
 Outputs: leaves your wallet (1000 sats); leaves your wallet (8500 sats);
 Fee: 500 sats at 2 sat/vB. No bump capability.

#### What to check
 
- The largest output of this transaction does not go to the requested recipient. 
- Read outputs from largest to smallest and account for every one. 

 
### An unusually high fee
 The wallet's summary: “This sends BTC” (review)
 
- 1 input needs your signature. 
- 2 outputs go outside this wallet; 0 return to you. 
 Inputs: yours (10000 sats);
 Outputs: leaves your wallet (8000 sats); change to you (1500 sats);
 Fee: 17000 sats at 850 sat/vB - far above the recommended rate. No bump capability.

#### What to check
 
- The fee is what the transaction pays the network, not what the site receives. 
- A fee rate far above the recommended rate is a signal to stop and reread. 

 Something wrong on this page? Open a prefilled issue in the documentation repository. What travels: the page path, the release this site describes, and your own words. Nothing about your wallet, transactions, or this browser is included or stored by this site.
 Page not helpful Stale screenshot Version mismatch Unsafe or unclear wording Broken journey

# Back up your recovery phrase | Universe Wallet

How to record the phrase so it survives fire, theft, moving house, and your own memory, and how to prove the backup actually works.

- Universe Wallet 
- Start here 
 
# Back up your recovery phrase

 Intended reader: anyone whose wallet holds, or will hold, anything they would mind losing.
 Goal: a physical record of the phrase that you can find in five years.
 Prerequisites: the wallet, your password, pen and paper, a private room.
 Safety: this is the highest-risk routine action in the whole product. Everything else can be
retried.

 
## The rule
 Section titled “The rule” 

 Your recovery phrase is the wallet. Not a hint, not a reset code. Whoever has the words has the coins.

 
 What the phrase carries: every account, every network, every address type, on any device and
in any BIP-39 compatible wallet. What it does not carry: your password, your connected
sites, your labels, contacts, frozen coins, and spending limits. Those are device settings and
have to be set up again after a restore.
 

 
## Where to write it
 Section titled “Where to write it” 

 Do Do not Pen on paper, or stamped metal Photograph it Two copies, in two separate places Store it in cloud notes, email, or chat Numbered, in order Type it into any website, ever Somewhere a house fire or a burglary would not reach both copies Store it in a password manager you do not control the sync of Somewhere someone you trust could find it if you could not Split it across services and hope 

 Order is part of the secret. Twelve correct words in the wrong order is not your wallet.

 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- Open Settings , then Export recovery phrase . 

- Enter your password. 

- Write the words on paper, numbered, in order. 

- Close the screen before you do anything else. 

- Put the paper where you decided it goes, now, not later. 

 
## How to verify the backup works
 Section titled “How to verify the backup works” 

 A backup you have never tested is a hope, not a backup.

 

- Note the first receiving address of your wallet. 

- In a separate browser profile, install the extension and restore from the paper copy alone. Do not
look at the screen version. 

- Confirm the same first address appears. 

- Remove that test wallet from the second profile. 

 If the address matches, your paper copy is correct and complete. If it does not, fix it while you can.

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 You can reconstruct the wallet from paper alone, with no device, no password, and no help.

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 What happens What it means The restored wallet shows a different address Usually a different address type, not a wrong phrase. Compare all four. See Address types . A word is illegible on the paper Rewrite the whole phrase from the wallet now, while you still can unlock it. You used a BIP-39 passphrase and did not record it The phrase alone is not enough. Record the passphrase separately, in a different place. 

 
## Recovery path
 Section titled “Recovery path” 

 While you can still unlock the wallet, every backup problem is fixable: open the export screen and
write it again. Once you cannot unlock it and the paper is wrong, there is no path. That asymmetry is
the whole reason to do this today.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Backup and recovery 

- If your wallet is compromised 

 Edit page Last updated: Nov 11, 2026

<!-- start/create-a-wallet/index.html -->

# Create a wallet | Universe Wallet

Generate a new 12-word wallet, choose a password, pick an address type, and finish the backup check before any money is involved.

- Universe Wallet 
- Start here 
 
# Create a wallet

 Intended reader: someone setting up their first Universe Wallet.
 Goal: a funded-ready wallet whose recovery phrase is written down on paper.
 Prerequisites: the extension installed. Pen and paper. Ten quiet minutes.
 Chain and network: all chains. Defaults to Bitcoin mainnet.
 Safety: the phrase you are about to see is the wallet. Nobody is keeping a copy.

 Do this where nobody can see your screen
 Not on a shared machine, not on a call, not while screen recording, not in a coffee shop with your
back to the room. A phrase seen once is a phrase gone forever.

 
 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- Open the extension and choose to create a new wallet. 

- Set a password. This encrypts the vault on this device. It is not recoverable and it is not
your backup. Use something long that you will still know in a year. 

- Read the recovery phrase. The wallet generates a 12-word BIP-39 phrase. Write the words on
paper, in order, numbered. Do not photograph it. Do not type it anywhere. 

- Pass the confirmation check. The wallet asks you to put selected words back in place. This
exists so that a phrase you never actually wrote down cannot silently become the only copy. 

- Choose an address type. Native SegWit is the default and is right for most people. If you are
going to hold inscriptions, read
 Payment and asset addresses first, because Taproot is where
artifacts conventionally live. 

- Finish. The wallet opens on an empty account. 

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 

- A wallet with one account, no balance, and an address you can receive to. 

- A paper record of 12 words, in order, stored somewhere you would still find after a house move. 

 
## How to verify
 Section titled “How to verify” 

 Before you put real money in, prove the backup works:

 

- Note your first receiving address. 

- Lock the wallet, or use a second browser profile. 

- Restore from the phrase you wrote down. 

- Confirm the same first address appears. 

 If a different address appears, either a word is wrong, the order is wrong, or the address type
differs. Fix that now, while the wallet is empty. See
 Backup and recovery .

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 

 What happens What it means What to do The confirmation check rejects your words The written copy does not match Start over rather than guessing. An empty wallet costs nothing to redo. You wrote the words but not the order BIP-39 order is part of the secret Redo the creation. Order matters. A restore shows a different address Wrong address type, not a wrong phrase, in most cases Switch address type and compare. See Address types . You closed the window before writing anything down Nothing is lost yet, because nothing is funded Delete the wallet and create a new one. 

 
## Recovery path
 Section titled “Recovery path” 

 While the wallet is empty, every mistake is free. That is the only time this is true, so use it. Once
funds arrive, the phrase on paper is the only path back.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Back up your recovery phrase 

- Backup and recovery 

- Locking and passwords

<!-- start/first-receive/index.html -->

# Receive for the first time | Universe Wallet

Get an address, check it in more than one place, and use a small test amount before anything that matters.

- Universe Wallet 
- Start here 
 
# Receive for the first time

 Intended reader: someone receiving into Universe Wallet for the first time.
 Goal: funds arriving at an address you control, confirmed on chain.
 Prerequisites: a wallet whose recovery phrase is already written down.
 Chain and network: any supported chain. Check the network before you share an address.
 Safety: an address sent to the wrong chain or network is money gone. Verify twice.

 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- Open the wallet and confirm the account and network shown at the top are the ones you mean. See
 Chains and networks . 

- Open Receive . 

- Copy the address, or show the QR code. 

- Send a small test amount first, from wherever the funds are coming from. 

- Wait for it to appear, then send the rest. 

 
## Verify the address before you use it
 Section titled “Verify the address before you use it” 

 Address confusion is the failure mode here, and it is silent.

 

- Check the first four and last four characters against what the sender sees, out loud if
possible. Clipboard-replacement malware changes the middle. 

- Check the prefix matches the network. A mainnet Bitcoin address starts bc1q , bc1p , 3 , or
 1 . Test network addresses look different. Sending mainnet coins to a testnet address, or the
reverse, does not bounce back. 

- Check the chain. A Bitcoin address is not a Dogecoin address. Nothing will warn the sender. 

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 The amount appears in your activity as pending, then confirms. Your balance goes up by the amount
sent, and the sender pays the fee.

 
## How to verify
 Section titled “How to verify” 

 

- The transaction appears under Activity with an increasing confirmation count. 

- The amount matches exactly. If it is lower, the sender paid the fee out of the amount, which is
their choice, not an error in your wallet. 

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 

 What you see What it means What to do Nothing arrives, but the sender has a transaction id The transaction exists and is unconfirmed, or went to a different address Look up the transaction id. Check which address it actually paid. Funds arrive but show as unavailable The coin was classified as asset-bearing, or is not yet confirmed See Protected outputs . The balance updates but assets do not Asset data comes from indexers and can lag behind the chain Wait, then see Troubleshooting . You sent to the wrong network The coins went to an address on a chain this wallet is not watching If you hold the keys for that chain in this phrase, you may be able to reach them. If not, they are gone. 

 
## Recovery path
 Section titled “Recovery path” 

 Receiving cannot lose funds that are already yours. The only irreversible mistake at this stage is
publishing an address that is not actually yours, which is why the verification step above exists.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Receive , including payment requests with an amount 

- Payment and asset addresses

# Send for the first time | Universe Wallet

Your first outgoing payment, done in the order that makes a mistake survivable, with the two facts about sending that surprise people most.

- Universe Wallet 
- Start here 
 
# Send for the first time

 Intended reader: someone making their first outgoing payment from Universe Wallet.
 Goal: an amount arriving at someone else’s address, with no asset spent by accident.
 Prerequisites: a funded wallet, a backed-up phrase, and the recipient’s address.
 Chain and network: Bitcoin mainnet in this example.
 Safety: this is irreversible. Nothing on this page can undo a confirmed transaction.

 Sending is behind a release gate
 The send and broadcast screens sit behind the bitcoin/send and bitcoin/broadcast gates. Whether
they work in your build was decided when that build was released, not by this documentation. If the
screen tells you the operation is not available in your build, it is not available, and no setting
changes that. See Why an action is unavailable .

 
 
## Two facts first
 Section titled “Two facts first” 

 

- Coins are spent whole. Paying 0.02 BTC from a 0.03 BTC coin does not leave that coin partly
spent. The whole coin is consumed and the remainder comes back to you as a change output. See
 Inputs, outputs, fees, change . 

- The fee follows size, not amount. Sending 10 BTC costs the same as sending 0.001 BTC if the
transaction is the same size in bytes. 

 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- Send a test amount first. Small enough that losing it would be annoying rather than serious. 

- Open Send , and confirm the account and network at the top of the screen. 

- Paste the recipient address. Compare the first four and last four characters against the source. 

- Enter the amount. 

- Choose a fee. See Choose a fee . 

- Read the review screen. Do not skim it. See
 Review a transaction . 

- Approve, or reject. Rejecting costs nothing. 

- Wait for the test amount to arrive at the other end and be confirmed. 

- Only then send the real amount. 

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 The transaction appears in Activity as pending, then gains confirmations. Your available balance
drops by the amount plus the fee. A change output returns to an address you own.

 
## How to verify
 Section titled “How to verify” 

 

- The recipient confirms arrival of the test amount. 

- Your activity entry shows the fee you chose, not a larger one. 

- Your total balance dropped by amount plus fee, and no asset you hold has moved. 

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 What you see What it means What to do Not enough available balance, though the total looks fine Some coins are protected and cannot fund a plain payment See Protected outputs . The transaction stays pending for a long time The fee rate was below what the network is currently clearing Wait. See the warning below about fee bumping. The change output is missing on the review The remainder is being paid entirely as fee Reject. Do not approve a transaction whose change line you cannot account for. The screen says the operation is not available in this build The release did not authorize it Nothing you can change. See Why an action is unavailable . 

 There is no way to speed up a stuck transaction from inside the wallet
 You can mark a transaction as replaceable when you create it, and that flag is off by default. But
Universe Wallet 1.7.5.8 has no fee bump, no speed up, and no child-pays-for-parent flow . Marking a
transaction replaceable does not give you a way to replace it here. If a payment is stuck, your
options are to wait, or to use separate software that can build a replacement. Choose the fee
carefully the first time.

 
 
## Recovery path
 Section titled “Recovery path” 

 There is none after confirmation. Before broadcast, rejecting the approval is free and complete. That
is why the review screen is the last real safety control you have, and why it is worth the thirty
seconds.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Send bitcoin 

- What a signature authorizes

# Import an existing wallet | Universe Wallet

Bring a wallet in from a recovery phrase or a private key, including the derivation-path presets for Unisat, Sparrow, Xverse, and Ordinals Wallet.

- Universe Wallet 
- Start here 
 
# Import an existing wallet

 Intended reader: someone moving an existing wallet into Universe Wallet, or adding a second one.
 Goal: your existing addresses and balances visible, at the same addresses you had before.
 Prerequisites: the recovery phrase or private key, and knowledge of which wallet it came from.
 Safety: typing a phrase is the moment you are most exposed. Confirm you are in the real extension
first.

 Check where you are typing
 Open the wallet from your own pinned toolbar icon. Never from a link, a pop-up window a page opened,
or a page that looks like the wallet. A page cannot see what you type into the extension. A fake
extension can see everything.

 
 
## What you can import
 Section titled “What you can import” 

 

 Source Supported 12 or 24-word BIP-39 recovery phrase Yes BIP-39 passphrase, sometimes called a 25th word Yes, entered alongside the phrase Custom derivation path Yes Private key, WIF or hex Yes, as a single-key wallet An address only, with no key Not through this flow. See Watch-only wallets . 

 
## Derivation presets
 Section titled “Derivation presets” 

 The same phrase produces different addresses under different derivation paths, which is why an
imported wallet can look empty when nothing is wrong. Universe Wallet offers presets that match how
other wallets derive.

 

 Preset Address types it offers Unisat Wallet Native SegWit, Nested SegWit, Taproot, Legacy, and two BIP-44 compatibility variants Sparrow Wallet Legacy, Native SegWit, Nested SegWit, Taproot Xverse Wallet Nested SegWit, Taproot Ordinals Wallet Taproot Other wallet All six variants 

 Universe Wallet scans the candidate paths and shows which of them have a balance or history, so you
can pick the one that matches your old wallet rather than guessing.

 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- Open the extension from your pinned icon. 

- Choose to import a wallet. 

- Enter the recovery phrase, in order. Add the BIP-39 passphrase if your old wallet used one. 

- Choose the preset for the wallet it came from, or set a custom derivation path. 

- Compare the addresses shown against an address you already know is yours. 

- Select the matching address type and finish. 

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 At least one address matches an address you used before, and the balance and history you expect
appear against it.

 
## How to verify
 Section titled “How to verify” 

 Take one address you have used in the past, and find it in the imported wallet. That single match
proves the phrase, the passphrase, the path, and the address type are all correct together. A balance
alone does not prove it, because a wrong path can still show an empty but valid wallet.

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 

 What you see Most likely cause What to do Wallet imports but shows zero balance Wrong derivation path or address type Try the preset for your old wallet, then the other address types. One word is not accepted It is not in the BIP-39 word list Check spelling. Many words differ only in the last letters. Addresses are close but not the same A BIP-39 passphrase was used and is missing Enter the passphrase. Without it, this is a different wallet entirely. Balance appears but assets do not Asset data comes from indexers, which can lag Wait, then check Troubleshooting . 

 
## Recovery path
 Section titled “Recovery path” 

 Importing is non-destructive to the source wallet. Your phrase still works everywhere it worked
before. If the import looks wrong, remove the imported wallet from Universe Wallet and try a
different path or address type. Nothing about a failed import can move your coins.

 After importing, that phrase now lives in two places
 Every additional place a phrase exists is another way to lose it. If your old wallet was on a device
you no longer control, treat the phrase as exposed and follow
 If your wallet is compromised .

 
 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Address types 

- Backup and recovery

# Install | Universe Wallet

Where the real extension is, which browsers can run it, which permissions it asks for, and how to check that what you installed is what you meant to install.

- Universe Wallet 
- Start here 
 
# Install

 Intended reader: anyone installing Universe Wallet for the first time.
 Goal: a working extension that came from the real listing.
 Prerequisites: a Chromium browser, Chrome 88 or later.
 Safety: installing a counterfeit wallet is the most common way people lose everything. Do not skip
the verification step.

 
## The only install route
 Section titled “The only install route” 

 The Chrome Web Store listing is
 Universe Bitcoin Wallet ,
item id fjalkkkbjffhgdoheannkodafhemfdba .

 Check that id in the address bar before you install. A counterfeit listing can copy the name, the
icon, the screenshots, and the description. It cannot copy the id.

 There is no other official distribution
 No archive from a chat message. No file from a support agent. No “beta build” behind a link in a
reply. No mirror site. If someone sends you a wallet to load manually, they are trying to take your
coins.

 
 
## Browser support
 Section titled “Browser support” 

 

 Browser Support Chrome 88 or later Yes. This is the target. The packaged extension declares Manifest V3 with a minimum Chrome version of 88. Edge, Brave, Opera, other Chromium browsers The same package runs on Chromium at that version or later. There is no separate store listing for them. Firefox Build targets exist in the source tree, but no Firefox listing is published. Treat Firefox as unavailable. Safari Not supported. Mobile browsers Not supported. Browser extensions do not run on mobile Chrome or mobile Safari. 

 
## Permissions it asks for
 Section titled “Permissions it asks for” 

 Every one of these is in the shipped manifest, and each has a narrow reason.

 

 Permission Why it is needed storage , unlimitedStorage Holds the encrypted vault, your settings, and cached asset data on your device. activeTab Lets a page you are on request a connection, only after you click the extension. declarativeNetRequest Applies the phishing policy that ships inside the extension. sidePanel Opens the wallet beside the page instead of as a popup. alarms Wakes the background worker so idle site connections expire on time. nativeMessaging , optional Requested only if you set up the Zcash companion. Not granted otherwise. Access to all sites A wallet cannot know in advance which site will request a connection. Nothing is read from a page until you approve that site. 

 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- Open the store listing and confirm the item id matches fjalkkkbjffhgdoheannkodafhemfdba . 

- Add the extension. 

- Pin it to the toolbar, so you always open the wallet from your own browser chrome rather than from
something a page drew. 

- Open the wallet, go to Settings , then About , and note the version number. 

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 The extension opens to a welcome screen offering to create a new wallet or import an existing one. It
holds no funds and no accounts yet.

 
## How to verify
 Section titled “How to verify” 

 

- The item id in the store URL matches the one above. 

- The version under Settings , then About , is one you can find in this documentation or in the
 release list . See
 Which version you are running for why that matters more than usual
here. 

- The extension icon in your toolbar is the one you pinned, and it is where you open the wallet from. 

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 

 What you see What it means What to do The listing name matches but the id does not A counterfeit listing Do not install it. Report the listing to the store. The browser says the extension needs a newer version Your browser is older than Chrome 88 Update the browser. A site offers to install the wallet for you Phishing Close the tab and install from the store listing yourself. The extension installs but the popup is blank Usually a stalled service worker See Troubleshooting . 

 
## Recovery path
 Section titled “Recovery path” 

 Nothing at this stage can cost you money: the wallet holds no keys yet. If you suspect you installed
something counterfeit, remove it, and do not enter any recovery phrase into it. If you already did,
treat it as a compromise and follow
 If your wallet is compromised immediately.

 
## Next
 Section titled “Next” 

 Create a wallet , or
 import an existing one .

# Holding your own keys | Universe Wallet

What self-custody actually transfers to you, the four irreversible facts it creates, and the habits that keep it survivable.

- Universe Wallet 
- Start here 
 
# Holding your own keys

 Self-custody means the keys that authorize spending exist only on your device, protected by a
password only you know, derived from a phrase only you hold.

 Nobody is holding a copy for you. Read that sentence twice, because everything below follows from it.

 
## The four facts
 Section titled “The four facts” 

 
### 1. There is no password reset
 Section titled “1. There is no password reset” 

 Your password unlocks one installation of the extension on one device. It is not an account
credential. There is no email link, no identity check, no support override. If you forget it, you
reinstall and restore from your recovery phrase.

 
### 2. The recovery phrase is the wallet
 Section titled “2. The recovery phrase is the wallet” 

 Those words are not a hint or a backup code. They mathematically are every key in the wallet. Anyone
who reads them owns everything they control, immediately and permanently, from anywhere.

 
### 3. A confirmed transaction is final
 Section titled “3. A confirmed transaction is final” 

 Once a Bitcoin transaction confirms, no one can reverse it: not you, not Universe, not the miner, not
the exchange on the other end. A wrong address is not a mistake you can appeal.

 
### 4. Nobody legitimate ever needs your phrase
 Section titled “4. Nobody legitimate ever needs your phrase” 

 Not support, not a verification step, not a wallet upgrade, not a giveaway, not an airdrop claim, not
a migration tool, not the person who says they are helping you recover it. There is no exception, and
there never will be. See Phishing and impostors .

 
## The habits that make this survivable
 Section titled “The habits that make this survivable” 

 

- Write the phrase on paper before you fund the wallet. Not in a screenshot, not in a note app, not
in a password manager sync you do not control, not in a message to yourself. 

- Fund it with a small amount first and move that amount out again, so you have practised the whole
loop before it matters. 

- Read the approval screen every time, even when you are sure. The one you skim is the one that was
different. 

- Keep a second wallet for connecting to applications you are trying for the first time, and keep
your long-term holdings out of it. 

 
## What Universe can and cannot do for you
 Section titled “What Universe can and cannot do for you” 

 

 Universe can Universe cannot Serve the balances and asset data the wallet displays See or store your recovery phrase, keys, or password Ship a build that refuses to spend an asset-bearing coin by accident Move, freeze, or return your funds Publish which operations a release authorized Reverse a transaction you signed Answer documentation and product questions Recover a lost phrase, for anyone, ever 

 Next: Which version you are running .

# Which version you are running | Universe Wallet

The published Chrome Web Store build is 1.0.13 from April 2025. This documentation describes the 1.7.5.8 source tree, which has not been published. Here is exactly what that means for you.

- Universe Wallet 
- Start here 
 
# Which version you are running

 There are two version numbers in play, and confusing them is the easiest way to be misled by this
site. This page exists so that you cannot be.

 
## The two numbers
 Section titled “The two numbers” 

 Published to users Described here Version 1.0.13 1.7.5.8 Date 15 April 2025 Not published Where Chrome Web Store item fjalkkkbjffhgdoheannkodafhemfdba The bitcoinuniverseio/wallet source tree Zcash support Predates it entirely Present in source Protocol operations authorized Not verifiable from this source tree 0 of 42 

 What this means for you
 If you installed Universe Wallet from the Chrome Web Store, you are running 1.0.13. Screens described
on this site may not exist in your build, may be laid out differently, or may behave differently.
Where this documentation and your wallet disagree, your wallet is correct . Never take an action
because a page here says a screen should be there.

 
 
## Why 1.7.5.8 is not published
 Section titled “Why 1.7.5.8 is not published” 

 Two independent blockers were recorded in the product’s release ledger. One is closed, one is not.

 

- No authorized artifact existed. This closed on 30 August 2026. A qualification campaign scoped
to Zerdinals and ZRunes completed against one candidate commit, every release gate passed, and an
authorization was produced covering thirteen operations across those two protocols and nothing
else. 

- The Chrome Web Store publishing credential is not available to the repository. This still
blocks submission. Nothing can be submitted regardless of readiness. 

 So an artifact that could be published exists, and it has not been published. Until it is, the wallet
people actually have installed is the April 2025 build.

 
## Why the committed source authorizes nothing
 Section titled “Why the committed source authorizes nothing” 

 The number above says 0 of 42, and that is not an
outage or an oversight.

 Authorization is not written into the source. It is attached at release time to one exact build, from
externally verified evidence covering the wallet, the API, the indexer, the network, confirmation, and
reconciliation. The baseline committed in the repository therefore authorizes nothing on purpose, so
that no build can inherit a claim it did not earn.

 The consequence for reading this site: a page describing a protocol action is describing a screen that
exists, not a screen that will work for you. See
 What this release authorizes and
 Why an action is unavailable .

 
## How to check your own build
 Section titled “How to check your own build” 

 

- Open the extension. 

- Go to Settings , then About . 

- Read the version shown there. 

 That number, and the screens you can actually reach, are the authoritative answer for you.

 
## What this site does with that
 Section titled “What this site does with that” 

 Every page carries a footer stating the release it was checked against and the date it was checked.
Anything that could not be verified in the 1.7.5.8 source is stated as unavailable
rather than described. The things that fell into that category are listed on
 Known limitations .

# What Universe Wallet is | Universe Wallet

A self-custody browser extension for Bitcoin, Dogecoin, Zcash, and Fractal Bitcoin, built so that coins carrying digital artifacts never fund an ordinary payment.

- Universe Wallet 
- Start here 
 
# What Universe Wallet is

 Universe Wallet is a browser extension that holds Bitcoin and Bitcoin-adjacent chains, and that
treats a coin carrying a digital artifact differently from a coin carrying only money.

 
## What it does
 Section titled “What it does” 

 

- Holds keys for Bitcoin, Dogecoin, Zcash, and Fractal Bitcoin , each with their test networks. 

- Generates keys on your device, encrypts them with a password you choose, and keeps them there. 

- Classifies every coin before spending, so an inscription or a token balance is not handed to a
miner as change. 

- Shows what leaves, what returns, and at what fee before you approve any signature, with a
confidence mark on every interpreted fact. 

- Grants a connected site one address on one network, for a window that expires. 

 
## What it is not
 Section titled “What it is not” 

 

- Not a custodian. Universe cannot move your funds, cannot reverse a transaction, and cannot
restore a recovery phrase you lost. That is the trade you made by holding your own keys. 

- Not an exchange or a broker. There is no buy button that takes your card, and nothing here is
investment advice. 

- Not a way to make chain activity private. Bitcoin addresses and amounts are public. See
 Privacy . 

- Not a guarantee that a protocol works. The wallet ships a protocol action only when the exact
build carries evidence for the whole path behind it. See
 What this release authorizes . 

 
## Who it is for
 Section titled “Who it is for” 

 Someone who owns digital artifacts on Bitcoin and wants to stop worrying that a routine payment will
quietly spend one of them. If you only ever hold plain bitcoin, a simpler wallet will serve you as
well, and this documentation will still be useful for the parts about reading a transaction.

 
## What to read next
 Section titled “What to read next” 

 

- Holding your own keys , if you have not done this before. 

- Which version you are running , which decides how much of this site
applies to you. 

- Install .

# Developer Integration Studio | Universe Wallet

Explore the generated provider contract, simulate every method, run the Compatibility Doctor, and download a working starter.

# Developer Integration Studio

 
# Developer Integration Studio
 Everything here is generated from the wallet's real provider surface - 45 methods, 6 events, namespaces tapwallet, tap_wallet, TapWallet, tapWallet, Tap_Wallet, universe, universewallet, UniverseWallet, bitcoinuniverse, bitcoinUniverse . The default playground runs a fake provider built from the contract: it reproduces shapes, events, and documented errors without contacting any wallet or network.
 This release authorizes 0 of 42 protocols. The simulation reproduces those refusals faithfully: methods whose protocol operation is unauthorized answer with the same error the real wallet gives, so your unavailable states get built against the truth.

# Redirecting to: /docs-wallet/help/support

<!-- tasks/activity/index.html -->

# Read your activity | Universe Wallet

What pending really means, how many confirmations to wait for, and what to do about a transaction that will not confirm.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Read your activity

 Intended reader: anyone waiting on a transaction, or checking what happened.
 Goal: correctly reading the state of your own money.
 Prerequisites: an unlocked wallet.

 
## The states
 Section titled “The states” 

 State Meaning Pending Broadcast, sitting in the mempool, not in a block. It can still be dropped. Confirmed Included in a block. Each new block adds a confirmation. Failed A failure was reported. Check the recorded evidence to distinguish a rejected request from an unknown outcome. 

 A timeout, interrupted page or error message alone does not establish that no funds moved or no fee
was paid. For a marketplace purchase, keep the existing execution or request reference and return to
that purchase to check its recorded status. Do not start a replacement purchase or clear wallet
storage to resolve an uncertain outcome. See
 Zcash market listings .

 
## How many confirmations
 Section titled “How many confirmations” 

 There is no universal answer, only a risk judgement.

 

- One confirmation is enough for a small payment between people who trust each other. 

- Three confirmations is a common threshold for ordinary amounts. 

- Six confirmations is the traditional benchmark for something you would mind losing. 

 An unconfirmed transaction is not a payment. If someone tells you they have sent funds and your wallet
shows pending, you have a promise, not money.

 
## When something will not confirm
 Section titled “When something will not confirm” 

 The fee rate was below what blocks are currently clearing.

 This wallet has no way to speed up a stuck transaction
 There is no fee bump, no speed up, and no child-pays-for-parent flow in Universe Wallet 1.7.5.8.
If a transaction is stuck, your options are: wait for the mempool to quieten, in which case it may
confirm eventually; or, if it was marked replaceable when you created it, build a replacement using
separate software that supports replacement. A transaction that is never mined is eventually dropped
by nodes and the coins become spendable again, but there is no fixed timetable for that.

 
 Marking a transaction replaceable at creation does not give you a control in this wallet for replacing
it later. That is why choosing the fee carefully the first time
matters more here than in wallets that offer a bump.

 
## Reading an entry
 Section titled “Reading an entry” 

 Each entry shows the amount, the direction, the fee, the counterparty address, and the transaction id.
The transaction id is the thing you can hand to anyone: it is public, it is verifiable independently,
and it does not reveal anything about your wallet beyond what the chain already shows.

 
## Where asset movements appear
 Section titled “Where asset movements appear” 

 Asset transfers appear alongside payments, subject to the wallet being able to read them. Asset data
comes from indexers, which read the chain and decide what a transaction meant. Indexers can lag behind
confirmations, so a confirmed transaction can briefly show a payment without its asset effect.

 If the wallet cannot read a protocol at all, the payment still appears and the asset effect does not.
See What this release authorizes .

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 What you see What it means What to do Pending for hours Fee below current clearing rate Wait. See the warning above. A transaction you do not recognise Either a change output you misread, or a real problem Check whether the destination is your own address. If not, go to If your wallet is compromised Confirmed but the asset has not moved Indexer lag, or an unsupported protocol Wait, then check Troubleshooting Activity is empty after a restore Wrong address type or derivation path See Address types 

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related”

<!-- tasks/choose-a-fee/index.html -->

# Choose a fee | Universe Wallet

What the presets mean, how to pick a custom rate, and why the choice matters more here than in most wallets.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Choose a fee

 Intended reader: anyone about to send.
 Goal: a transaction that confirms in the time you need, without overpaying.
 Prerequisites: a send in progress.
 Safety: picking too low is not recoverable inside this wallet. Read the warning.

 
## What you are choosing
 Section titled “What you are choosing” 

 Not an amount. A rate , in satoshis per virtual byte. The wallet multiplies that rate by the size
of the transaction it built to get the fee. See
 Inputs, outputs, fees, change .

 Two payments of the same value can carry very different fees, because one spends more coins than the
other and is therefore physically larger.

 
## The presets
 Section titled “The presets” 

 The wallet offers live presets alongside a custom option. In the source they are labelled Standard,
Fast, Instant, and Custom, ordered from cheapest and slowest to most expensive and quickest.

 

 Preset Use it when Standard Nothing is waiting on this. Hours are fine. Fast You want it in the next few blocks. Instant It is time-sensitive, or the mempool is busy and you cannot wait. Custom You have a specific rate in mind and know why. 

 Presets are computed from current network conditions, so their sat/vB values move. The number shown
at the moment you approve is the one that applies.

 
## Setting a custom rate
 Section titled “Setting a custom rate” 

 Enter the rate in sat/vB. The review screen shows the resulting fee amount before you approve, so you
can check the arithmetic against your expectation.

 A rate below what blocks are currently clearing will sit unconfirmed for a long time, possibly
indefinitely if the network stays busy.

 Choose carefully, because there is no fee bump here
 Universe Wallet 1.7.5.8 has no fee-bump, speed-up, or child-pays-for-parent flow. A transaction sent
at too low a rate can only be waited out, or replaced using separate software. This is different from
wallets that let you raise the fee afterwards, and it is the single most important thing to know
before choosing a rate.

 
 
## When the fee looks too high
 Section titled “When the fee looks too high” 

 Almost always because the transaction has many inputs. Check the input list on the review screen. A
payment funded from twenty small coins is large and therefore expensive, regardless of the amount.

 Options:

 

- Send a different amount, so a smaller set of coins covers it. 

- Use coin control to select fewer, larger coins where the flow allows it. See
 Coin control . 

- Wait for a quieter period, if the payment is not urgent. 

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 The review screen shows the fee as an amount and a rate. After broadcast, the activity entry shows the
same fee.

 
## How to verify
 Section titled “How to verify” 

 Compare the fee on the review screen with the fee in your activity entry. They should match exactly.
If the confirmation is slower than the preset suggested, that is network behaviour, not a wallet
error: a preset is an estimate of conditions, not a promise.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Send bitcoin 

- Review a transaction

<!-- tasks/coin-control/index.html -->

# Coin control | Universe Wallet

Where manual coin selection actually exists in this build, what the locked-coins and coin-health screens show, and what is not available.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Coin control

 Intended reader: someone who wants to decide which coins fund a transaction.
 Goal: control over selection, or a clear understanding of where you do not have it.
 Prerequisites: an unlocked wallet.
 Safety: selecting the wrong coin is how an artifact gets spent. The protection described in
 Protected outputs is what stops that on the default path.

 Where manual selection exists, and where it does not
 In Universe Wallet 1.7.5.8, manual coin selection is offered inside the PSBT approval flow , where
a request lets you choose which of your coins fund it. There is no standalone coin control screen 
that lets you pick inputs for an ordinary send before you build it. If you were expecting a general
purpose coin picker on the send screen, it is not there.

 
 
## What is there
 Section titled “What is there” 

 
### Locked coins
 Section titled “Locked coins” 

 A screen listing the coins currently held back from ordinary payments, and why each one is held. It
has no protocol gate, so it is present regardless of what your build authorizes. This is the screen to
open when your available balance is lower than your total and you want to know which coins account for
the difference.

 
### Coin health
 Section titled “Coin health” 

 An overview of the shape of your coin set: how many coins you hold, how they are distributed, and how
much is protected. Useful before a large payment, because a wallet made of many small coins produces
large, expensive transactions.

 
### Manual selection during PSBT approval
 Section titled “Manual selection during PSBT approval” 

 When a signature request allows it, the approval screen offers a selector for which of your coins fund
the transaction. Protected coins are excluded from that selector unless you are in a flow built for
moving that asset.

 
### Consolidation
 Section titled “Consolidation” 

 A consolidation screen exists, combining many small coins into fewer larger ones. It sits behind the
 bitcoin/send gate, so its availability depends on your build.

 
## Why you would consolidate
 Section titled “Why you would consolidate” 

 Fees follow transaction size, and size follows the number of inputs. A wallet holding fifty small
coins pays much more to make a payment than a wallet holding three large ones.

 Consolidating during a quiet, low-fee period is cheaper than being forced to consolidate during a busy
one.

 Never consolidate blindly
 Consolidation touches many coins at once, which is exactly the operation that can sweep an
asset-bearing output into a payment if protection is not doing its job. Read the input list on the
review screen before approving a consolidation, and confirm no protected coin appears in it.

 
 
## Locking a coin yourself
 Section titled “Locking a coin yourself” 

 You can mark a coin as locked, which keeps it out of ordinary payments the same way an asset-bearing
coin is kept out. Locks are device settings: they do not travel with your recovery phrase, and a
restore will not bring them back.

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 

- You can see which coins are held back and why. 

- Where a flow offers selection, you choose which coins it uses. 

- Consolidation, where available, reduces the number of coins you hold. 

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 What you see What it means No coin picker on the send screen Correct for this build. Selection is offered in the PSBT approval flow, not the send flow. A coin you want to spend is not selectable It is protected. See Protected outputs . Consolidation says it is not available in this build The bitcoin/send gate is not authorized in your release 

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Protected outputs 

- Inputs, outputs, fees, change 

- Review a PSBT 

 Edit page Last updated: Nov 11, 2026

# Connect an application | Universe Wallet

Approve a site's connection request, choose the idle window, and check the one line on the screen that a hostile page cannot forge.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Connect an application

 Intended reader: anyone using a site that wants to talk to the wallet.
 Goal: the site able to see one address and ask for signatures, and nothing more.
 Prerequisites: an unlocked wallet and a site that requested a connection.
 Safety: connecting cannot move funds. Connecting to an impostor site is still how signature
attacks begin.

 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- On the site, choose to connect a wallet, and pick Universe Wallet. 

- The wallet opens an approval window. 

- Read the origin line. It comes from the browser, not from the page. A page can print any brand
it likes in its own body; it cannot change this line. 

- Confirm the account and network being offered are the ones you want the site to see. 

- Choose the idle window : 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, which is the default, or until you
disconnect. 

- Approve, or reject. 

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 The site shows you as connected and can read the address you selected. It appears in your
 Connected sites list with its granted scope and last-used time.

 
## How to verify
 Section titled “How to verify” 

 

- The origin in your address bar matches the origin shown by the wallet. 

- The site displays the address you expected, and no other. 

- The connection is listed under Connected sites . 

 
## What it can and cannot do afterwards
 Section titled “What it can and cannot do afterwards” 

 Granted: reading one address on one network, reading the public data at that address, and asking you
for signatures.

 Never granted: your recovery phrase, your private keys, moving a coin without a fresh approval, your
other accounts and networks, or the contents of pages you visit.

 See Connection permissions for the whole boundary.

 
## Choosing the idle window
 Section titled “Choosing the idle window” 

 It is an idle timer, not an age limit. Every use restarts it.

 

- 24 hours for a site you are trying once. 

- 7 days for something you use occasionally. 

- 30 days , the default, for a site you use regularly. 

- Until you disconnect only for a site you genuinely rely on and would notice going wrong. 

 Shorter is safer, and the cost of it expiring is one extra approval.

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 

 What you see What it means What to do The site says connected, the wallet does not list it The page is faking a connection state Leave. Do not sign anything. The approval window did not appear The extension service worker may be asleep Open the extension from your toolbar, then retry The origin does not match the address bar You are on an impostor page, or in a frame you did not expect Reject and close the tab The site asks you to connect again every visit The idle window is short, or you are in a private window Choose a longer window if you trust it 

 
## Recovery path
 Section titled “Recovery path” 

 Reject at any time. If you already connected and regret it, open Connected sites and disconnect.
Disconnecting stops new requests; it does not undo a signature you already gave. See
 Manage connections .

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Connection permissions 

- Provider API

# Hardware wallets | Universe Wallet

Keystone is the one hardware integration present in this build. Ledger and Trezor are shown as coming soon and cannot be connected.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Hardware wallets

 Intended reader: someone who wants keys held on a dedicated device rather than in a browser.
 Goal: signing on hardware, with the extension used only to build and broadcast.
 Prerequisites: a Keystone device.
 Safety: verify every address and every amount on the device screen , not in the browser.

 
## What is available
 Section titled “What is available” 

 Device State in this build Keystone Connectable. Air-gapped QR, and USB. Ledger Listed, and disabled. The connect control shows coming soon and cannot be used. Trezor Listed, and disabled, the same way. Any other device Not integrated. Use the watch-only flow and sign elsewhere. 

 The hardware feature is marked experimental in the product itself
 Verify addresses on the device. Start with a small amount and complete the whole loop, receive, send,
and confirm, before you move anything significant onto it.

 
 
## Why hardware helps
 Section titled “Why hardware helps” 

 The private keys stay on a device that has no browser, no extensions, and no web pages. Even a fully
compromised computer cannot extract them. What it can still do is show you a transaction that is not
what you think it is, which is why the device screen matters more than the browser screen.

 
## Steps, Keystone
 Section titled “Steps, Keystone” 

 

- Open the wallet and add a hardware wallet. 

- Choose Keystone. 

- Connect over USB, or scan the QR sequence the device shows for the air-gapped path. 

- Select the account and address type. See Address types . 

- Verify the first address shown in the extension against the device screen. 

 
## Signing
 Section titled “Signing” 

 

- Build the transaction in the extension as usual. 

- The extension hands it to the device, over USB or as a QR sequence. 

- Read the transaction on the device screen. Amount, destination, fee. 

- Approve on the device. 

- Return the signature to the extension, which broadcasts it. 

 The device screen is the one that counts
 A compromised computer can show you one destination in the browser and pass a different one to the
device. The device screen is outside that computer’s control. If they disagree, the device is right
and you should reject.

 
 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 A wallet whose keys are on the device. The extension can build transactions and show balances, and
cannot sign anything on its own.

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 What you see What it means What to do Ledger or Trezor is disabled, reading Coming soon Not implemented as a connection in this build Use Keystone, or watch-only The device is not detected over USB Browser permission, cable, or firmware Try the air-gapped QR path instead Addresses differ between device and extension Address type or derivation path mismatch Fix before receiving anything The QR sequence will not complete Screen brightness, camera focus, or a partial scan Restart the sequence from the beginning 

 
## Recovery path
 Section titled “Recovery path” 

 A hardware wallet has its own recovery phrase, held by the device, not by Universe Wallet. Losing the
device is survivable if you have that phrase. Losing the phrase is not, exactly as described in
 Backup and recovery .

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Watch-only wallets 

- Known limitations

# Inspect a Lightning invoice | Universe Wallet

Read invoice details without sending a payment.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Inspect a Lightning invoice

 This flow belongs to the unreleased Wallet source candidate. It is not a claim
that your installed store release supports Lightning payments.

 Open Send Lightning , paste a BOLT11 invoice into Invoice to inspect ,
then choose Inspect invoice . Review the decoded details and choose
 Save inspection to retain the result in this wallet’s local operation history.

 Inspection does not contact the invoice recipient or send money. An expired
invoice or an unsupported required feature can be inspected, but its result
must not be treated as permission to pay. The result explicitly distinguishes
inspection from payment submission.

 A saved node address, connection configuration or app policy also does not
prove a live Lightning connection. Payment requires a connected engine and
its separate approval and settlement checks. That complete payment journey
has not been verified for this candidate.

 Edit page Last updated: Nov 11, 2026

# Locking and passwords | Universe Wallet

What the password actually protects, how to set the auto-lock window, and what changing a password does and does not do.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Locking and passwords

 Intended reader: everyone.
 Goal: a wallet that is locked when you are not using it, with a password you will still know.
 Prerequisites: an unlocked wallet.

 
## What the password protects
 Section titled “What the password protects” 

 It encrypts the vault on this device . Someone with access to your unlocked computer cannot open
the wallet without it.

 
## What it does not do
 Section titled “What it does not do” 

 

- It is not your backup . Losing it does not lose your funds, as long as you have the recovery
phrase. 

- It does not protect the recovery phrase anywhere else. Anyone with your phrase does not need
your password. 

- It cannot be reset. There is no account, no email link, no support override. If you forget it, you
reinstall and restore from the phrase. See
 Backup and recovery . 

 
## Auto-lock
 Section titled “Auto-lock” 

 Settings , then Lock time . The range runs from 30 seconds to 4 hours, with a default of 30
minutes.

 

 Your situation Suggested Shared or public computer 30 seconds to 5 minutes Personal laptop you carry 5 to 15 minutes Home machine only you use 30 minutes, the default Large holdings, anywhere Shorter than feels convenient 

 You can also lock immediately from the wallet menu, which is worth doing every time you step away.

 
## Changing your password
 Section titled “Changing your password” 

 Settings , then Password . You need the current one.

 Changing it re-encrypts the vault on this device. It does not change your recovery phrase, your keys,
your addresses, or anything on any chain. A password change is not a response to a phrase compromise:
if your phrase was exposed, the password is irrelevant, and you need
 If your wallet is compromised .

 
## Choosing one
 Section titled “Choosing one” 

 Long beats complicated. Four or five unrelated words you can picture will outlast a short string of
symbols you will forget. Do not reuse a password you use anywhere else, because the compromise of an
unrelated service should not reach your wallet.

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 

 What you see What it means What to do Password rejected and you are sure it is right Keyboard layout, caps lock, or a similar-looking character Type it into a plain text field first to see it Forgotten entirely Not recoverable Reinstall and restore from the phrase The wallet locks constantly Auto-lock is set very short Raise it, within reason The wallet never seems to lock It locks on the timer, not on tab close Use the immediate lock when you step away 

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Security dashboard 

- Backup and recovery
