# Manage connections | Universe Wallet

Identify connected sites by origin and chain, read the displayed connection state, and verify that revocation was saved.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Manage connections

 Intended reader: anyone who has connected sites, which is anyone who has used a marketplace.
 Goal: a connection list you recognise, with nothing on it you cannot account for.
 Prerequisites: an unlocked wallet.
 Safety: disconnecting cannot retract a signature or transaction already delivered.

 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- Open Connected sites . 

- Read the exact origin and displayed chain for each entry. A site name or icon is not its identity. 

- Disconnect anything you do not recognise, or no longer use. 

- If you use a group revoke action, check the result for each affected site. 

- Wait for the wallet to confirm that removal was saved. Reload the wallet’s connection list and
verify that the unwanted entry is gone. 

 
## What the list tells you
 Section titled “What the list tells you” 

 

- Origin. The exact website origin reported to the wallet. 

- Chain. The chain shown on the connection card. 

- Signature status. The card shows Signed or Unsigned . This does not replace reviewing
a new signature request. 

- Connection state. The card shows Active or Stored only for the saved record. 

- Expiry. Read the expiry text displayed for that connection. 

 Universe Wallet also scores connections for risk locally, on your device, and offers to revoke risky
sites in one step.

 
## Housekeeping worth doing
 Section titled “Housekeeping worth doing” 

 

- Disconnect anything you tried once and never returned to. 

- Disconnect anything whose origin you do not recognise. 

- After finishing a trade or a mint, disconnect the site. Reconnecting takes one approval. 

- Review the list after anything unexpected happens. 

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 After the wallet confirms removal, the origin should be absent from a successfully refreshed list.
The disconnected site must request access again. A failed save or read does not establish that
access ended.

 
## What disconnecting does not do
 Section titled “What disconnecting does not do” 

 A successfully saved disconnect ends the site’s saved wallet access. It does not:

 

- reverse a transaction you approved, 

- revoke a signature you already gave, including a partial signature someone can still complete, 

- remove an offer from a marketplace’s order book. 

 See What a signature authorizes for why that
distinction matters, especially for listings.

 If you are here because something went wrong, disconnect first, then go to
 If your wallet is compromised .

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 

 What you see What it means What to do A site you do not recognise You connected and forgot, or a page you visited requested it Disconnect. Then check activity for anything you did not authorize. The connection list cannot be loaded Current permissions could not be read Retry the read. A load error is not an empty permission list. Disconnect or revoke fails Removal has not been confirmed Retry, then reload the wallet list. Treat access as unresolved until the saved result is verified. A site reappears after disconnecting Removal may not have been saved, or a new connection was approved Check the saved result and read any new approval before accepting it. A site still shows you as connected on its own page Its display may be stale Confirm removal in a successfully refreshed wallet list, then reload the site. 

 Keep wallet storage intact while resolving a failed permission read or write. If the failure
continues, use support .

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Connection permissions 

- Security dashboard

# Receive | Universe Wallet

Get an address, create a payment request with an amount and a note, and understand what appears while a payment is still unconfirmed.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Receive

 Intended reader: anyone being paid.
 Goal: funds arriving at an address you control, on the network you meant.
 Prerequisites: an unlocked wallet with the intended account and network selected.
 Safety: the risk here is publishing the wrong address, not losing what you already have.

 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- Confirm the account and network shown at the top of the wallet. 

- Open Receive . 

- Copy the address, or show the QR code for someone to scan. 

- Optionally set an amount and a note. The wallet encodes those into the QR code and into a
copyable link, so the sender’s wallet can pre-fill them. 

- Share it. 

 
## Verify before sharing
 Section titled “Verify before sharing” 

 

- Compare the first four and last four characters of the address against what the recipient sees.
Clipboard-replacement malware changes the middle and leaves the ends plausible. 

- Check the prefix matches the network . See
 Payment and asset addresses . 

- Check the chain . A Bitcoin address is not a Dogecoin address and nothing will stop a sender
trying. 

 
## Address reuse
 Section titled “Address reuse” 

 Reusing one address works and links every payment to it publicly. Using a fresh address per payment
is better for privacy and makes no difference to safety. See Privacy .

 
## Which address to publish
 Section titled “Which address to publish” 

 

 You are receiving Use Plain bitcoin Your default receiving address, Native SegWit unless you changed it An inscription or ordinal Your Taproot address, unless the sender specifies otherwise From a service that rejects bc1 Your Nested SegWit address, starting with 3 

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 The payment appears under Activity as pending, then confirms. Your balance rises by the amount
sent. The sender pays the fee unless they chose to take it out of the amount.

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 

 What you see What it means What to do Nothing arrives, sender has a transaction id It went somewhere, possibly not to you Look up the id and check which address it paid It arrives but the balance is unavailable Unconfirmed, or classified as asset-bearing See Protected outputs Balance updates, assets do not Asset data comes from indexers and can lag Wait, then see Troubleshooting Amount is less than agreed The sender took the fee out of the amount Not a wallet problem. Ask the sender. 

 
## Recovery path
 Section titled “Recovery path” 

 Nothing about receiving can lose funds you already hold. If you published an address that was not
yours, the funds went to whoever owns it, and there is no recall.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Receive for the first time 

- Read your activity

<!-- tasks/review-a-psbt/index.html -->

# Review a PSBT | Universe Wallet

How to read a partially signed transaction someone else built, which sighash flags change what you are agreeing to, and when to refuse outright.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Review a PSBT

 Intended reader: anyone approving a signature request that came from a site rather than from the
send screen.
 Goal: knowing what the finished transaction can become, not just what it looks like now.
 Prerequisites: a pending PSBT approval.
 Safety: a PSBT is a transaction that someone else wrote. Everything on it was chosen by them.

 
## What a PSBT is
 Section titled “What a PSBT is” 

 A partially signed Bitcoin transaction is a draft that can carry some signatures and be completed
later. Marketplaces and applications use them because a trade needs inputs from two people who are
never online at the same moment.

 The important consequence: you are signing something you did not construct . The inputs, the
outputs, the fee, and the flags were all chosen by whoever sent it.

 
## What the wallet shows you
 Section titled “What the wallet shows you” 

 What you are about to sign Origin app.example Your input 7c9b…:0 (protected, inscription) Leaves your wallet 1 inscription Comes back to you 0.04000000 BTC Signature scope SIGHASH_SINGLE | ANYONECANPAY Fee Paid by the other party 

 The screen lists every input and output, marks which inputs are yours, marks which of your inputs are
protected, and computes the net effect on your wallet. A manual input selector is available inside
this flow when the request allows you to choose which of your coins fund it.

 
## The line that decides everything
 Section titled “The line that decides everything” 

 Signature scope. This is the sighash setting, and it determines what your signature commits to.

 Scope You are agreeing to SIGHASH_ALL The whole transaction, exactly as shown. Nothing can change without invalidating your signature. SIGHASH_SINGLE | ANYONECANPAY Only your input and one matching output. Everyone else can still change their part. SIGHASH_NONE Your input, and no output at all. Whoever completes it decides where the money goes. 

 A partial signature is an open offer, and it does not expire
 If the scope is not the whole transaction, anyone holding your signed fragment can complete it, on
their own terms, at any time, for as long as that coin stays unspent. Removing a listing from a
marketplace does not revoke it. The only real cancellation is to spend the coin yourself into a
transaction you control.

 
 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- Read the origin at the top. Confirm it is the site you are actually using. 

- Read what leaves and what comes back . Compare against the price you were quoted. 

- Read the signature scope . If it is not the whole transaction, decide whether you are willing to
leave an open offer standing. 

- Check whether any of your protected coins are being spent, and whether that is what you meant. 

- Check the fee and who pays it. 

- Check for anything marked UNKNOWN . 

- Approve, or reject. 

 
## Refuse outright when
 Section titled “Refuse outright when” 

 

- The scope is SIGHASH_NONE . There is almost no legitimate reason for a wallet to be asked for that. 

- The amount coming back does not match the price you agreed. 

- A protected coin is being spent and you did not start an asset sale. 

- The origin is not the site you are on. 

- The wallet could not decode part of the request. 

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 The source candidate checks that selected signing inputs belong to the current account and that the
returned approval still matches the reviewed transaction. Changing accounts or networks, locking the
wallet, or revoking the requesting site can invalidate an unexecuted approval. If that happens,
return to the current request and review it again; do not broaden the selected inputs to bypass a
refusal. These checks do not establish that every hardware or website integration is available.

 Approving returns your signature to the requesting site. It does not necessarily broadcast anything:
the site may hold your signature until a counterparty completes the transaction.

 
## How to verify
 Section titled “How to verify” 

 Check your activity. A PSBT you signed may not appear as a transaction until it is completed and
broadcast by the other party. That gap is normal, and it is also why a partial signature deserves more
thought than a payment: there may be no immediate evidence of what you agreed to.

 
## What the transaction inspector is not
 Section titled “What the transaction inspector is not” 

 Universe Wallet has a transaction inspector that looks up a transaction by its id. It is a lookup
tool for transactions that already exist. It does not decode or review a PSBT. The approval screen
is the place where a PSBT is reviewed.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- What a signature authorizes 

- Coin control 

- Protected outputs

<!-- tasks/review-a-transaction/index.html -->

# Review a transaction | Universe Wallet

How to read the approval screen in the order it is built, the four lines that matter most, and the ones that should make you reject.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Review a transaction

 Intended reader: anyone about to approve anything.
 Goal: understanding what you are authorizing before you authorize it.
 Prerequisites: a pending approval on screen.
 Safety: this is the last point at which the outcome is still up to you.

 The approval screen is stacked in a fixed order, and the order is deliberate. Read it from the top.

 
 Blocking problems come first, then what actually happens to your money, then the overall status,
then non-blocking warnings, then the full detail. Reject sits beside Approve at the same size.
 

 
## The four lines that matter most
 Section titled “The four lines that matter most” 

 Even in a hurry, read these four.

 What you are about to sign Leaves your wallet 0.03450000 BTC Comes back to you 0.01446152 BTC Network fee 0.00003848 BTC at 18.5 sat/vB Assets touched None 

 

- What leaves. Not what you typed. What the transaction actually spends. 

- What comes back. Your change. If this is missing or much smaller than you expected, the
difference went to the fee. 

- The fee. Stated once, in one place, as an amount and a rate. 

- Assets touched. If this is not “none” on a payment you intended to be plain money, stop. 

 
## Reading it in full
 Section titled “Reading it in full” 

 
### Blocking
 Section titled “Blocking” 

 A check that failed hard. Approve stays disabled and you cannot click through it. This is not advice;
it is a refusal.

 
### Impact
 Section titled “Impact” 

 What leaves, what returns, the net change, and any assets touched. Every line carries a confidence
mark of EXACT , ESTIMATED , or
 UNKNOWN . See
 Confidence marks .

 
### Status
 Section titled “Status” 

 Ready, Review, or Blocked. It can never read Ready while any fact on the screen is unknown.

 
### Warnings
 Section titled “Warnings” 

 Things worth knowing that do not block: address reputation notes, decoded risk rows, advisories. Each
risk row is labelled Warning or Critical in words, not only by colour.

 
### Details
 Section titled “Details” 

 Network and account, the destination and whether it is external to your wallet, the fee, every input
and output, which inputs are protected, and the raw transaction so you can inspect it elsewhere.

 
## When to reject
 Section titled “When to reject” 

 Reject, without hesitating, if any of these is true.

 

- The change output is missing and you cannot account for the remainder. 

- The destination is not the address you expect, character for character at both ends. 

- An amount is larger than you intended, in any line. 

- Anything is marked unknown. 

- The origin shown is not the site you think you are on. 

- A protected coin is being spent and you did not deliberately start an asset transfer. 

- You do not understand what the transaction does. 

 Rejecting costs nothing
 No fee is paid. Nothing is broadcast. Nothing is recorded on chain. You can always ask the site to
try again. The only cost of rejecting is a few seconds; the cost of approving wrongly is permanent.

 
 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 Approving broadcasts the transaction and moves you to a result screen with a transaction id. Rejecting
closes the request and tells the requesting site you declined.

 
## How to verify afterwards
 Section titled “How to verify afterwards” 

 

- The activity entry shows the same amount and the same fee you saw on the review. 

- Your balance dropped by amount plus fee, and nothing else moved. 

- Any asset you hold is still listed. 

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- What a signature authorizes 

- Review a PSBT 

- Inputs, outputs, fees, change 

 Edit page Last updated: Nov 11, 2026 

 Previous Choose a fee Next Review a PSBT

<!-- tasks/security-dashboard/index.html -->

# Security dashboard | Universe Wallet

What the security dashboard tracks, what it can tell you, and the limits of what any dashboard can see.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Security dashboard

 Intended reader: anyone doing a periodic check of their own setup.
 Goal: knowing whether your wallet’s posture matches what you intended.
 Prerequisites: an unlocked wallet.
 Safety: the dashboard reports. It does not defend. Acting on what it says is the part that matters.

 
## Where it is
 Section titled “Where it is” 

 Settings , then Security . The screen has no protocol gate, so it is present regardless of what
your build authorizes.

 
## What it tracks
 Section titled “What it tracks” 

 

- Recovery status. Whether you have confirmed a backup of your recovery phrase. 

- Login history. When the wallet was unlocked. 

- Session log. What happened during recent sessions. 

- Phishing URL checking. A place to check a URL against the wallet’s phishing policy before you
visit it. 

- Connection risk. Local scoring of your connected sites, with a one-step way to revoke risky
ones. 

 Everything here is computed on your device. None of it is a report sent anywhere.

 
## A monthly ten-minute check
 Section titled “A monthly ten-minute check” 

 

- Open the dashboard and read the recovery status. If it does not say your phrase is backed up,
go to Back up your recovery phrase . 

- Read the login history. Anything you cannot account for is worth investigating. 

- Open Connected sites and remove anything you no longer
use. 

- Check your auto-lock timer is short enough for how you actually work. See
 Locking and passwords . 

- Confirm your paper backup is still where you think it is, and still legible. 

 
## What a dashboard cannot see
 Section titled “What a dashboard cannot see” 

 

- Whether your recovery phrase has been copied. A phrase read from paper leaves no trace anywhere. 

- Whether a signature you gave was a good idea. It can tell you what you signed, not what it
meant. 

- Whether an outstanding partial signature can still be completed by someone. See
 What a signature authorizes . 

- Anything happening in another wallet using the same phrase. 

 A clean dashboard is reassuring and it is not proof. Treat it as one input.

 
## Optional controls worth turning on
 Section titled “Optional controls worth turning on” 

 Universe Wallet includes optional per-transaction and daily spending caps, and an address whitelist.
They are off by default, because most people do not want them and a wallet that demands configuration
before it is safe is a badly designed wallet. If your holdings are significant, they are worth the
five minutes.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Security model 

- If your wallet is compromised

<!-- tasks/send/index.html -->

# Send bitcoin | Universe Wallet

Make an outgoing payment, understand the replaceable flag, and know what the wallet does not offer if the transaction gets stuck.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Send bitcoin

 Intended reader: someone making a payment out of the wallet.
 Goal: the right amount reaching the right address, with no asset spent by accident.
 Prerequisites: available balance, the recipient address, an unlocked wallet.
 Chain and network: shown at the top of the wallet. Check it.
 Safety: irreversible once confirmed. There is no fee-bump flow to rescue a mistake.

 Sending is behind a release gate
 The send and broadcast screens sit behind the bitcoin/send and bitcoin/broadcast gates. Whether
they are usable in your build was decided at release time. If the screen states the operation is not
available in this build, that is authoritative. See
 Why an action is unavailable .

 
 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- Open Send . 

- Confirm the account and network at the top. 

- Enter the recipient address, or pick one from your address book. 

- Enter the amount. The wallet spends from the available pool only, never from protected coins. 

- Choose a fee rate. See Choose a fee . 

- Optionally mark the transaction replaceable . Read the section below before you rely on it. 

- Read the review screen in full. See Review a transaction . 

- Approve, or reject. 

 
## The replaceable flag
 Section titled “The replaceable flag” 

 Universe Wallet lets you mark a transaction as replaceable when you create it, and the flag is off
by default . The review screen states which way it is set.

 Marking a transaction replaceable does not give you a way to replace it
 Universe Wallet 1.7.5.8 has no fee bump, no speed up, and no child-pays-for-parent flow . The flag
records that the network may accept a replacement; it does not add a control in this wallet for
building one. If your payment is stuck, your options are to wait, or to construct a replacement using
separate software that supports it. Do not send at a low rate on the assumption that you can raise it
later.

 
 The flag also has a privacy and counterparty effect: some recipients treat a replaceable unconfirmed
transaction as not yet received, and will wait for a confirmation before crediting you.

 
## Batch sending
 Section titled “Batch sending” 

 A batch send screen exists, paying several recipients in one transaction. It sits behind the same
 bitcoin/send gate as an ordinary payment, so its availability depends on your build. Batching is
cheaper than separate payments because the fee follows total size rather than the number of
recipients.

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 The transaction appears in Activity as pending, with the fee you chose, then gains confirmations.
Your available balance falls by amount plus fee, and a change output returns to an address you own.

 
## How to verify
 Section titled “How to verify” 

 

- The recipient confirms arrival. 

- The fee in your activity matches the fee you approved. 

- Every asset you held is still listed. 

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 What you see What it means What to do Insufficient funds while the total looks sufficient Protected coins cannot fund a plain payment See Protected outputs Fee looks unreasonably large Many small inputs are being consolidated, so the transaction is big Review the input list. Consider sending less, or a different coin selection. No change output on the review The remainder is being paid as fee Reject unless you meant it Stuck pending for hours The rate was below what blocks are currently clearing Wait. See the replaceable section above. Screen says not available in this build The release did not authorize the operation Nothing you can change locally 

 
## Recovery path
 Section titled “Recovery path” 

 Before approval: reject. It is free and complete.
After confirmation: none exists.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Send for the first time 

- Coin control 

- Inputs, outputs, fees, change 

 Edit page Last updated: Nov 11, 2026

<!-- tasks/sign-a-message/index.html -->

# Sign a message | Universe Wallet

What message signing proves, why the wallet has no screen for composing one yourself, and why raw data signing is off by default.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Sign a message

 Intended reader: anyone asked by a site to sign a message.
 Goal: proving you control an address, without agreeing to something you did not read.
 Prerequisites: a connected site that requested a signature.
 Safety: no coin can move from signing a message. That does not make every message safe to sign.

 Message signing is initiated by a site, not by you
 Universe Wallet 1.7.5.8 has no screen for composing your own message and signing it . Message
signing appears only as an approval, in response to a request from a connected application. If you
need to sign an arbitrary message for your own purposes, this wallet does not currently offer that.

 
 
## What a message signature proves
 Section titled “What a message signature proves” 

 That the holder of a private key agreed to a specific piece of text. It is used to prove address
ownership without moving funds: sign in to a service, claim membership of a collection, verify you
control an address to a counterparty.

 No fee is paid. Nothing is broadcast. No coin can move as a direct result. 

 
## Why it still deserves attention
 Section titled “Why it still deserves attention” 

 A message is not always a neutral proof. It can be a statement, an agreement, or a term. What the text
says is what you are agreeing to, and the wallet cannot know which sentences carry weight.

 The wallet scans message text for scam-language patterns and warns you when it finds them, which
helps with the obvious cases and cannot help with a well-written one. Read the text yourself.

 
## The three variants you may see
 Section titled “The three variants you may see” 

 Request What it is What to do Text signing Human-readable text Read every line before approving Raw data signing A hex blob, not readable text Off by default. See below. Multiple message signing Several messages in one request Each one still counts. Read them all, or reject. 

 Raw data signing is off by default, and enabling it needs a typed confirmation
 A blob you cannot read is indistinguishable from something you would never agree to. That is exactly
why it is disabled until you deliberately turn it on. If a site insists you enable it, that is a
reason to leave, not a reason to comply.

 
 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- The site requests a signature and the approval window opens. 

- Read the origin shown by the wallet. It comes from the browser, not from the page. 

- Read the message text in full. 

- Confirm the address being used is the one you intend to prove ownership of. 

- Approve, or reject. 

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 The signature is returned to the requesting site. Nothing appears in your activity, because nothing
happened on the chain.

 
## Refuse when
 Section titled “Refuse when” 

 

- The message is unreadable, or is raw data you did not expect. 

- The message contains terms you would not agree to in writing. 

- The origin is not the site you are on. 

- The request arrived without you doing anything on the page. 

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- What a signature authorizes 

- Phishing and impostors 

 Edit page Last updated: Nov 11, 2026 

 Previous Review a PSBT Next Connect an application

# Switch chain and network | Universe Wallet

Change which chain and network the wallet is showing, and understand what that does to connected sites and to your addresses.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Switch chain and network

 Intended reader: anyone using more than one chain, or testing on a test network.
 Goal: the wallet showing the chain and network you intend to act on.
 Prerequisites: an unlocked wallet.
 Safety: acting on the wrong network is how funds go somewhere unrecoverable. Check before you copy
an address.

 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- Open Settings , then Network . 

- The screen lists every network the build knows about, and states how many are selectable. 

- Choose one. Entries a build has not enabled are marked Coming soon and cannot be selected. 

- Confirm the network name now shown at the top of the wallet. 

 
## The list
 Section titled “The list” 

 Ten networks appear: Bitcoin, Bitcoin Testnet, Bitcoin Testnet4 (Beta), Bitcoin Signet, Dogecoin,
Dogecoin Testnet, Zcash, Zcash Testnet, Fractal Bitcoin, and Fractal Bitcoin Testnet. See
 Chains and networks for what each is for.

 
## What changes
 Section titled “What changes” 

 

- The addresses shown, because formats differ per network. 

- The balance, assets, and activity, because they are read per network. 

- Which protocol operations are conceivable, because authorization is recorded per protocol and per
network. 

 
## What does not change
 Section titled “What does not change” 

 

- Your recovery phrase. One phrase covers every network. 

- Anything on any chain. Switching is a view change, not a transaction. 

- Existing connections. A connection is granted for one address on one network, and switching does
not extend it to another. A site that needs the other network has to request it. 

 
## A site can ask you to switch
 Section titled “A site can ask you to switch” 

 An application can request a chain or network switch, and the wallet shows an approval for it. Read
which network is being requested before approving, particularly if you were not expecting the prompt.

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 The wallet header shows the network you chose, and the balance and assets are those of that network.

 
## How to verify
 Section titled “How to verify” 

 

- The network name in the wallet header is the one you selected. 

- The receiving address has the prefix you expect for that network. 

- The balance matches what you expect for that network, which for a test network is usually zero until
you use a faucet. 

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 

 What you see What it means What to do Balance is zero after switching Correct. That network holds nothing yet. Switch back, or fund it An entry is marked Coming soon The build did not enable that network Nothing you can change locally A connected site stops working Its grant was for the other network Reconnect on the network you are using A switch prompt appeared unexpectedly A page requested it Read the network being requested. Reject if unclear. 

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Chains and networks 

- Connection permissions

<!-- tasks/watch-only/index.html -->

# Watch-only wallets | Universe Wallet

What the cold-wallet import actually is in this build, where its entry point lives, and what you cannot do with it.

- Universe Wallet 
- Everyday tasks 
 
# Watch-only wallets

 Intended reader: someone who wants to watch an address without holding its keys in the browser.
 Goal: visibility of balances and assets with no signing capability present.
 Prerequisites: the extended public key of the wallet you want to watch.
 Safety: a watch-only wallet cannot spend. That is its entire value.

 
## What it is
 Section titled “What it is” 

 A cold wallet import brings in public key material only . The wallet can derive addresses, show
balances, show assets, and build unsigned transactions. It holds nothing that can authorize a spend.

 Two limits worth knowing before you start
 

- The import takes an extended public key , presented by QR from an air-gapped device. There is no
flow in this build for typing or pasting a single address to watch. 

- The entry point is behind developer mode , which you enable by tapping the version number in
the About screen repeatedly. It is not on the ordinary setup path. 

 
 
## What it is for
 Section titled “What it is for” 

 

- Watching cold storage. Keys stay on a device that never touches a browser; the extension shows
you what is there. 

- Preparing transactions offline. Build the transaction in the browser, sign it elsewhere, then
broadcast. 

- Reducing exposure. Nothing in the browser profile can move those funds, so a compromised browser
is a privacy problem rather than a loss. 

 
## Steps
 Section titled “Steps” 

 

- Open Settings , then About , and enable developer mode by tapping the version repeatedly. 

- Add a wallet, and choose the cold wallet option. 

- Scan the extended public key QR from your signing device. 

- Confirm the derived addresses match the ones your signing device shows. 

 
## Expected result
 Section titled “Expected result” 

 A wallet entry that shows balances and assets, and that offers no path to sign a transaction. Any
attempt to spend produces an unsigned transaction for you to sign elsewhere.

 
## How to verify
 Section titled “How to verify” 

 Compare the first derived address against what your signing device displays. If they differ, the
derivation path or account index does not match. Do not receive to an address you have not verified on
the signing device itself.

 
## Common failures
 Section titled “Common failures” 

 What you see What it means What to do No cold wallet option Developer mode is not enabled Enable it in About Addresses do not match the device Wrong derivation path or account Recheck the path on the signing device Balance is zero but the device shows funds Different address type or path See Address types 

 
## Recovery path
 Section titled “Recovery path” 

 A watch-only wallet holds nothing to lose. Remove it and re-import at any time. Your funds are
governed entirely by the device holding the keys.

 
## Related
 Section titled “Related” 

 

- Hardware wallets 

- Security model
